Śakra, Tribindu, Mūrdhāna, and Niṣedha—by these it is adorned.
This ninth, supreme pada should be known as consisting of twenty-seven syllables.
When the wise one has bound the Rāvinī mudrā while under the power of the Pitṛs...
Then the practitioner of mantra attains union by reciting it once;
O Supreme Goddess, this is due to the power of this threefold word:
*mahārāva* joined with fire (*ra*), adorned with the womb (*i*) and the bindu (*m*).
Again, [place] the *haṃsa* within a fire-enclosure (*vahnipuṭa*), further adorned with the *bindu*,
*kāla*, and *agni*; then, join the *nāda* mounted upon the fire to the creation (*sṛṣṭi*).
One should give *amṛta* alone, [the syllable] *varuṇa* adorned with fire (*ra*),
preceded by *kāla* (*ha*) and pervaded by the *praṇava* (*oṃ*). Then *gaṇendra* situated in air (*ya*), joined with *mukhadāruṇā* (*va*), and [finally] *varuṇa* conjoined with the womb (*bhaga*).

The tenth word, O Goddess worshipped by the gods, is formed by adding the letter *ca* (cāpādya), followed again by the letter *ni*, marked with three vowels (*nisvara*), and then the syllable *da*. This word consists of ten syllables;
it bestows all prosperity, is the essence of all things, and brings about the descent of great fortune.
When one recites [the mantra] one thousand times while the lotus of the heart remains undisturbed through the restraint of the fluctuations of the mind, then one shall attain good fortune.
O Goddess, that good fortune which belongs to the Giver of Wealth (Kubera) would bring about such desire.
Having extracted Varuṇa (va) three times, joined with Mukhadāraṇā (i),
and conjoined with Bindu (m) at its head, one should again extract the first of the sixth [group] (ṣa).
Then the head of Vahni (ra), the third of the three (e), and the seventh of the fifth [group] (pa).
One should extract the first of the sixth [group] situated upon the first of the fifth [group], the double-tongued [Ṣa] residing in Varuṇa [Va],
its head pressed down by the goad [A], and Indra [Sa] adorned with the goad [A]. Then one should extract Kāla [Ka] grown upon the fifth [group] and ending in Bhairava [Ha].
The first [syllable] of the third [group] is the established effect; it is infinite and situated within fire.
It is firmly rooted in Kālāgnirudra and rests upon the crown of the Bindu.
This twelve-syllabled word is remembered as the eleventh.
It is proclaimed as all-pervading, auspicious, and the bringer of peace and nourishment.
One should meditate upon the goddess there, flowing with nectar, within that wheel of the twelve terminal digits (*kalās*) which has been celebrated as being like the moon.
O Goddess, one should then cause the Person to flood the hollow of the heart-lotus;
by this path of yoga, one nourishes the world in an instant.
Again, having extracted the *tāraka* (the nasal bindu), one should extract the fifth [consonant] together with the seventh,
joined with the bow (*cāpa*) and the goad (*aṅkuśa*), and then extract the *kāla* (the letter *ka*) alone. Furthermore, the first of this [same group] is likewise joined with the *kāla* and the goad.
One should extract the Fire [Ra] alone, situated at the beginning of the fifth [vowel].
Varuṇa [Va] should be given together with the goad [U]; one should extract Haṃsa [Ha] alone.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, it should be joined with three dots [M] and preceded by the Yoni [Ā].
The eleventh has been indicated; the twelfth is the supreme state (*pada*).
And that which follows from the flow of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) is the highest state.
By means of that practice of extension (*āyāma*), it is the state that bestows the three abodes.
This essence bestows all accomplishments and brings about freedom from old age and death.
When this word is recited, omniscience shall arise.
Having placed the *marmman* within the fire and marked it with the *modanī* and the *bindu*.
Furthermore, the King of Mantras (the practitioner) should cause [the mantra] to be bestowed according to the true measure:
having extracted the *haṃsa* alone situated in the fifth *marman*,
and having joined the *haṃsa* with the goad (*aṅkuśa*), it should again be given as a whole.
Then, one should have the letter *ka* (kāla) and the letter *la* (*kuṇḍala*) joined together with effort.
Then there is the seed-syllable of fire (*ra*) alone, conjoined with the horse (*a*) and the goad (*ṅa*).
It should end with Varuṇa (*va*), be solitary, and marked by the three vowels of negation (*i*).
Then [one should take] Kāla joined with Praṇava, which is infinite and absolute;
having extracted Śakra alone, it is infinite and situated in Kāla.
The head is traversed by the three vowels, and Varuṇa likewise is twofold.
Adorned by that very [seed-syllable] on its head, it is the first of the *yoni* [syllables] located at the beginning of the fifth;
then the first of the bow [syllables] alone, and again the one ending with Varuṇa alone.
The prohibition [syllable], traversed by the goad, is located at the beginning of the fifth of the prohibitions.
One should place [the letter] situated in fire (ra), and then extract the first of the time-syllables (ka). Again,
one should take the infinite (a) alone, and further, the horse (ha) adorned with three vowels.
Again, one should place this *kāla* (the letter *ka*) and then the solitary *bhāskara* (the letter *ra*).
Having correctly placed the solitary *vāyu* (the letter *ya*), one should extract the solitary *candra* (the letter *sa*).
Place the *vahni* (the letter *ra*) mounted upon *gaṇendra* (the letter *ga*) and marked with the abode of *vahni* (the letter *ra*).
One should extract the arm conjoined with Kāla (the letter *ka*) and adorned with the three vowels (*i*, *u*, *ṛ*);
first there should be the Yoni alone, followed by the arm pierced by the goad (*aṅkuśa*).
Then one should again extract Śakra (*la*), topped with the three vowels, which is the very first of all.
The first of the sixth [group] alone is again the nectar situated in time;
situated above the seventh vowel is the first of the fifth [group] with three suns;
O Goddess of the Gods, it is joined with the bindu, and the first of the third [group] is accompanied by the goad.
Having extracted Indra alone, one should extract Vāyu alone. O Bhairavī, the first [syllable] of the third [group] should be given three times, along with the visarga.
Having placed the Nāda within the Fire (Ra), it is struck on the head by the Aṅkuśa (U).

One should contemplate the thirteenth word, which bestows the fruit of all accomplishments: the *bindu* joined with the head (*m*), enclosed by fire (*ra*), and fallen at the end of the lunar [syllable *sa*]. 13.209–210ab.
O Goddess of the Mind, this has been proclaimed in fifty-one verses; by its mere recollection, it destroys all defects of epilepsy. Through its incense, collyrium, and ointment, it dispels epilepsy.
O fortunate one, by the mere remembrance of one who dwells in the cremation ground, the unsurpassed state arises;
O Supreme Goddess, there is an incomparable threefold *melāpa*.
Now, what is the use of saying more? By the bearing of this very state—
There is nothing that the King of the Foot, once accomplished, does not always perform.
Then, O Goddess, one should extract the god Sadāśiva threefold.
Furthermore, O Mahāmohalakṣmī, one should correctly bestow [the mantra] three times:
the Great Roar (Mahārāva) mounted on Fire (Vahni), adorned with the Yoni and the Bindu.
It should be given three times, O Maheśānī; then one should extract the "double-tongued" (Dvijihva) once more.

One should give the letter *ma*, which is joined with the fifth [vowel *u*], ascended [to the top], adorned with the *bindu* and *nāda*, and conjoined with the moon (*caṃdra*) and creation (*sṛṣṭi*). Then again, the sixth [vowel *ū*] alone;
and having extracted the fire (*vahni*) alone, conjoined with *kāla* and the *aṅkuśa*.

Having extracted the fire (*vahni*) alone from the seventh [letter] mounted upon itself, as well as the fifth and so forth in their entirety; having likewise extracted the moon (*candra*) in two parts along with the goad (*aṅkuśa*);
and [placing] the fire joined with the goad, preceded by the womb (*yoni*), in its entirety.
One should extract the syllable beginning with *amṛta* (A), blazing with fire (R), and radiant with three vowels (Ā, I, U).
Then one should again extract the sixth [vowel] alone, and once more the [sixth vowel] alone. Having extracted *kāla* (M) alone, and then the one preceded by *yoni* (V) alone.
Indra should be depicted with a goad and marked with the vowel *ī*;
Varuṇa should be joined with a goad; and Soma should be adorned with the three vowels (*i*, *ī*, *u*).
One should extract Kāla as being alone, conjoined with that [Soma] and marked with the *niṣedha*.
One should extract the syllable joined with *nāda*, having two tongues and marked by delusion (*mohana*);
then Varuṇa joined with the goad (*aṅkuśa*), followed by the sixth [vowel] situated in the wind (*vāyu*).
One should extract the wind alone, its head constricted by the goad.

O Maheśvarī, at the end of the word, one should apply three times the Yoni-mantra, which is preceded by the Vahni (Ra), resplendent with three vowels, situated in the Western quarter (Va), the Great Nectar (Sa), the Lotus (U), and struck by the Elephant-goad (K). O Goddess, one should employ it thus threefold at the conclusion of the word.
Again, having extracted the letter *ka* (kāla), joined with the *nāda*;

then *va* (varuṇa) as it is pervaded by the three vowels; then the third letter (*ga*) preceded by a vowel (*svarātmaga*); then that which is endowed with the abode of fire (*vahni-geha*, i.e., *ra*); and then *bhairava* alone.
The syllable preceded by *yoni* (the letter *i*) and ending with *śūla* (the letter *m*), its head pressed down by the *aṅkuśa* (the letter *u*),
topped with the three vowels of fire (*e*), and adorned with that very same [letter] upon the horse (*a*).
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, the *nāda* joined with *nāda* should be given in two parts:
[the syllable] *ra* (fire) with the *aṅkuśa* (anusvāra) on top, followed by *va* (Varuṇa) marked with the three vowels (*ai*),
and then *ha* (horse) accompanied by that same [syllable], joined with the *kāla-aṅkuśa* (the letter *kṣa*).
The fifth letter [Pa] joined with the first [A], situated in fire [Ra], pierced by the bindu at its head;
O Goddess of the gods, it is accompanied by the goad [Sa]. Then the Haṃsa, adorned with the three vowels [Ā, Ī, Ū], is again extracted three times along with the visarga, O Maheśvarī.
The syllable *Amṛta* (A) mounted upon *Varuṇa* (U), with the second vowel (*Ī*) as its crest;
this word, joined with *Nāda* (M) and *Nāda* (H), is of great power.
This fourteenth word is to be known as consisting of sixty-four syllables.
It destroys all untimely death, brings about peace and prosperity, and is auspicious;
it removes the faults of the great samaya and destroys all mixtures of impurities. It is supreme for unsealing what has been sealed and bestows accomplishment through a single recitation.
O Bhairavī, even for a slayer of a Brahmin, this bestows liberation merely by its recitation;
if the practitioner should remember this word in whatever manner,
O Goddess of gods, it is said to grant success and supernatural powers accordingly.
Even if the entire universe were filled with Brahmins who had committed every possible sin,
that transgression is destroyed by the mere single utterance [of this mantra].
When one recites it within the lotus of the heart for even a single month, O Lord, [the sins are likewise destroyed].
Then the gods and goddesses bestow the state of dream-like knowledge;
the Yoginīs of the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvar, and Svar remain under his control.
Through the assembly of the gods, the great *melāpaka* perfection arises.
O Goddess, by the power of this foot, there is no doubt in this matter:
there is no accomplishment here that is not achieved by this very [mantra].
Therefore, one should bestow Sadāśiva and extract his essential form.
Furthermore, O Queen Mahāmāyā, [the mantra consists of] only the last letter of Varuṇa,
preceded by the Yoni, situated in the fifth position, and only the first letter of the third [vowel].

One should place between these two the letter *aśva* (ha), adorned with three vowels (*i*, *u*, *m*), situated at the end of the trident (*śūla*) and preceded by the womb (*yonipūrva*). Then, place it again in the fifth position.
One should further give the letter *aśva* (ha) with three vowels above it, preceded by the third vowel (*u*).
The horse situated at the vital point (marmasthita) should be extracted, its head pressed by the goad (aṅkuśa).
Then one should extract Indra, whose head is pressed by three vowels. The goad should be preceded by the womb (yoni); one should again extract the end of this.
Then, having again extracted *kāla* (the letter *ka*) joined with *nāda*,
one should again provide the *yoni* (the letter *i*) preceded by it, and likewise the pure *amṛta* (the letter *sa*) at the beginning.
Having again extracted the first of this (*sa*), one should extract the pure fire (*ra*).
O Goddess, one should bestow [the seed-syllable] three times: the letter *gha*, established in the womb of the letter *a* and the like, with its crown surmounted by the three vowels;
likewise, the horse (*a*) joined with that same [vowel], placed in fire (*ra*), and surmounted by the bindu and the goad (*a*). One should cause it to be given in this threefold manner.
One should extract only the syllable *kāla* (ka) joined with the goad (*aṅkuśa*, i.e., *ū*).
Then there is the syllable joined with fire (*ra*) and the house (*e*), ending with Varuṇa (*va*) and situated therein.
It has the three vowels of fire (*rī*) at its head, possesses two tongues (*jha*), and is situated with the letter *sa*.
In the abode of fire, one should extract the solitary Vāyu from the conjoined [syllables].

O fortunate one, one should then cause that very same [Vāyu]— which is mounted upon Agni as the first of the sixth [group] and adorned with Yoni as the first of Kāla— to be imparted in its solitary state.
O Mahātapa, this is declared to be the seven-word and thirty-three-syllable *pada* beginning with Gaṇendra, Varuṇa, and Pañcamādya Trisūryaka.
This fifteenth word is the pacifier of all misfortune.
When one remembers this mantra at the junction of the three abodes,
then omniscience arises for the practitioner, O Great Goddess.
The eightfold group beginning with *aṇiman* (atomicity) constantly precedes him. O fortunate one, worldly enjoyments resort to the practitioner by mere remembrance, just as bees flock to honey.

O Great-minded One, subjugation, attraction, inciting enmity, killing, expulsion, and so forth, are perfectly accomplished simply by the recollection of this word, which is worshipped by the gods. Therefore, [meditate] again upon the god Sadāśiva, O you who are honored by the gods.
Below the *bindu* and *nāda* is the fire, the well-compacted *kālāgni*.
[One should contemplate] Ananta together with fire, situated within *kālāgni* and endowed with the *bindu*.
The first of the fifth [vowels], accompanied by Varuṇa (*va*), has its head pierced by the *bindu*.
One should extract the nectar (Amṛta) mounted on the fifth [vowel], followed by the fire (Vahni) alone.
Then the first of the sixth [group] accompanied by Rudra, again the fire alone,
the wind (Samīraṇa) alone, and the negation (Niṣedha) situated at the beginning of the fifth.
This fulfillment of the mantra must be performed while remaining established in the fire;
having extracted only the letter *ka* together with the arrow and the excellent bow.
O beautiful woman of the gods, one should give the *niṣedha* adorned with three dots (*tribindu*).
Again, [one should take] *kāla*, the *kevalin*, and *nāda* accompanied by *nāda*.
Again, one should extract *samīraṇa* joined with *nāda* and followed by *kāla*.
O Maheśānī, [the mantra] is marked with the *yoni* at the beginning, followed by the fifth [vowel] preceded by fire (*ra*),
studded with three suns (*r*) at the head, and adorned with the *praṇava* (*oṃ*).
It begins with the *yoni*, is solitary, possesses two tongues (*ha*), and is the prohibitor (*kṣa*).

One should again extract the *niṣedha* (the letter *m*) with its head stepped upon by three vowels; it should be marked by that [vowel]. Then one should extract Varuṇa (*va*) alone, Gaṇeśa (*ga*) alone, the first of the fifth [group] (*pa*) together with the goad (*ś*), and Kāla (*ka*) alone.

One should further extract Vāyu joined with Yoni, then Mahākāla; Nāda joined with Nāda, and Kāla conjoined with Aṅkuśa. [Then] the first of the fifth [group] situated in the seventh, and the first of Kāla conjoined with the eighth.
Extract only the fire (ra) and the seventh syllable of the water (ya), which is the pause;
then place Varuṇa (va) at the end of that and make it into a single cluster again.
Then give the third syllable along with the fire (ra) and the three dots (m).
One should again extract the [syllable] situated at the vital point (*marman*) of the horse, joined with the womb (*yoni*).
Having extracted the first of this [mantra] once more, one should again place the horse along with its vital points.
Only the trident (*triśūla*) should be given, and the horse should again be placed within the moon.
Whatever is marked should be given increased by three and joined with three.
Furthermore, that which is situated in the bow and so forth, being overcome by the goad, is prohibited;
however, having extracted what is situated in the bow and so forth, the Lord of Knots is struck by the Discus-bearer.
Having again extracted the first of this [mantra], which is devoid of the supreme goad (paramāṅkuśa),
O Goddess of Gods, there is again a negation (niṣedha) whose first part is marked by three vowels.
This negation is pervaded by the three vowels, followed by the sound (nāda) and the sun (vahni) alone.
Having combined the sound *na* with the fifth vowel, and having placed the letter ending in *gha* within the womb (*yoni*) and so forth,
and being adorned with the letter *ā*, one should extract the fire alone.
Endowed with the three vowels and beautified by that very [vowel],
join it with Varuṇa and place him at its end.
Endowed with the goad and illuminated by that very [vowel], [join] Agni.
One should give Varuṇa (va) endowed with three vowels and adorned by that very same [vowel];
one should give the double-tongued (śa) alone and the wind (ya) alone.
The double-tongued (śa) should be given three times in the first of the fifth [group], situated in the fifth.
O illustrious lady, one should extract the *praṇava* three times along with the *visarga*;
at the end, the *pada* joined with *nāda*, extracted as the tenth part,
consisting of seventy-three syllables, which pierces the seven netherworlds.

O Goddess, O Bhairavī, wherever this word is uttered by the practitioner exactly as it is, there the yantras situated in the netherworld (pātāla) are shattered. When the practitioner utters the mantra while stationed at the Wheel of Gold (hāṭakacakra), [the same occurs].

O Goddess of gods, as many as a thousand women— agitated, tormented by hunger and longing for remembrance— come before the illustrious face of the practitioner, concentrated during the festival of lamps.
They approach the best of practitioners, afflicted by hunger and the pain of their memory.
Having honored the best of practitioners, they lead him to the supreme city;
there the practitioner shall live for an entire kalpa, O beautiful one.
This king of mantras, even when unaccomplished, is remembered as the performer of all rites.
But, O Goddess, once this has been accomplished, there is nothing that it cannot achieve.
This essential state is declared to bestow all prosperity.
Furthermore, the *mottanī* should be given, and immediately thereafter, the *kāla*.
Nāda joined with nāda, Kāla adorned by nāda,
Samīraṇa joined with Yoni, and restrained by Bhīma-śaṅku.
This seventeenth word is declared to consist of six syllables. When the practitioner, having ascended the knot of Māyā, recites this word,
then he shall accomplish all rites by uttering it but once.

One should accomplish the piercing (*vedhana*), as well as the paralyzing (*stobha*), of many Śakra-nets and even hundreds of nets of delusion within the ritual vessels and other implements. Furthermore, one should perform the great deluding (*mahāmohanī*) rite upon the double-tongued [serpent] struck by the hook (*aṅkuśa*).
That which resides within Bhairava should be given; then again, the negation alone.
That which ends with Varuṇa should be alone, preceded by the Yoni and accompanied by Puṇya.
Then Sadāśiva should be given, obstructed by Bhīma and Śaṅku.
Where the *puṇyonā* [mantra] has been bestowed, there one should cause the three-syllabled [mantra] to be given.
This eighteen-syllabled *pada* has been proclaimed by me as seven-syllabled.
Having properly placed it within the enclosure of the heart, one should employ it through the battle against hatred.
O Goddess, this which has been proclaimed is the bestower of knowledge, which completely destroys all doubts; it performs every action, O Goddess,
when it is mounted upon the fire-syllable (Ra) and adorned with the Yoni and the Bindu.
The double-tongued [Sa], situated within Bhairava [Ha], with its head marked by the Yoni [I];
having extracted the solitary Vāyu [Ya], it is adorned with Fire [Ra] as the first of the sixth;
the first of Kāla [Ta] joined with the Yoni [I], and Rāva [Ū] pierced by the Yoni [I].
This nineteen-syllable word, consisting of seven letters, is known as "Bhīma" (or "Śaṅku"), with the *bindu* conjoined to its head and obstructed by the *nirodhinī*.
By means of this, the lord of practitioners always attains a dear union.
When one recites this mantra at the Kuṇḍalinī-cakra,
then one shall accomplish everything that is established within the three worlds.
Furthermore, [the syllable] Mahāmohanī, the double-tongued [Ha],
covered by Mohanā [Ū], Varuṇa [Va] alone, and the first of the third [group] [I] alone;
preceded by Yoni [E], situated in its own place [S], mounted on Vahni [Ra], and with Yoni [E].
One should extract *varuṇa* (va) together with the end of *varuṇa* (u), joined into a single syllable (*vu*).
Then one should provide *vahni* (ra) adorned with three dots (*m*), followed by *sadāśiva* (sa).
After that, one should provide *bhīmaśaṅku* (kṣa); this is the nine-syllabled word.
This is declared to be the twentyfold [mantra] which bestows success upon one situated in the wheel of life.
O Goddess, when the Mountain recites this pada in that wheel,
he then attains immortality and becomes an omniscient practitioner.

One should extract the *rāva*, the *yoni*, the *bindu*, and the fire (*vahni*) together in one place. The first of the sixth [vowel] is conjoined with the *aṅkuśa*, and the first of the fifth [vowel] is alone.
That which precedes the *yoni* should be accompanied by the *aṅkuśa*, and the negation (*niṣedha*) should be placed at the beginning of the fifth.
Furthermore, one should again extract its very first letter at the beginning.
One should likewise form the "Yoni" (V) preceded by the "Sound" (A), adorned with three vowels; that is the Fire (Ra). One should extract only the "Time" (Ka).
The sound (na) joined with the sound (da), Varuṇa (va) marked with three vowels;
the double-tongued one (dvi-ji-hva, i.e., *li*) mounted upon the seventh (*sa*), Kāla (ka) situated at the beginning of Kāla (*k*);
the head [of the syllable] conjoined with the goad (aṅkuśa, *u*), and Vāyu (ya) adorned with three vowels.
One should then extract Sadāśiva, conjoined with that *niṣedha* (prohibition).
That station, restrained by *Krodhaśaṅku*, is of great power;
it is declared to be the twenty-first [syllable], joined with the twenty-second letter.
The auspicious mantra named Pāpabhakṣaṇa, which removes all sins—
O Goddess, there is no transgression that it would not purify.
O Goddess of the gods, by remembering the Supreme situated in the Pure Abode,
one reduces to ashes even great sins such as the uprooting of a *liṅga*.
Furthermore, it is solely the prohibition [of such acts] that is overcome by the Supreme Goad.
Furthermore, O Goddess, one should extract that very same [syllable] joined with the bow (cāpa);
it should be known, O Īśvarī, as bestowing bliss even when not yet accomplished.
Again, Mahāmāyā, bestowing [the fruit], should extract only Kāla.
One should employ Mahānāda joined with Nāda, followed by the third vowel alone;
then Aśva situated at the vital point (marmasthita), Praṇava together with Samīraṇa,
Gaṇeśa accompanied by Yoni, and finally that which resides in Varuṇa.
One should extract the Fire (Ra) with three vowels as its head (Ū), and again the End-maker (Ma).
Then the Sound (Ha) joined with Sound (Ha), followed by the sixth vowel (Ū) preceded by the first (A) and conjoined with the fifth (U).
Again, the Fire (Ra) situated in Rudra (E), and finally the Nectar (Sa) preceded by the first (A) alone.
One should extract Antaka first, together with the Praṇava; then one should extract Dvijihva. One should extract Niṣedha, which is mounted by the three vowels, and then extract Antaka again.
Furthermore, one should extract Nāda joined with Nāda, and then extract Gaṇendra once more.
One should place Vahni situated in Rudra, and then again a mere mallet (musala).
Then one should extract the incomparable Kāla with a goad (aṅkuśa) from the fifth [position], together with the womb (yoni);
likewise, one should extract Agni as a prohibition (niṣedha) conjoined with a goad.
Having extracted only the *vāyu*, one should extract only the *haya*;
then again, having reached the limit of the ears, one should extract only the *śakra*.
One should fashion a horse [seal] joined with a bow and a goad, adorned with the three vowels;
likewise, one should extract the syllable *bala* alone.
Furthermore, it should be situated in a non-vital part (*amarmasthita*), preceded by the womb-syllable (*yonipūrva*), and accompanied by the goad.
The fifth [vowel] and the first [consonant], joined with the wind [letter] and struck on the head by the goad;
having extracted the pure wind [letter], which is the horse resplendent with three vowels;
again, the first of time [the letter *ka*] alone, and the first of the bow [the letter *ca*] conjoined with fire.
The letter joined with the womb (yonisaṃyukta) should be placed first; then again, the one beginning with time (kālādya), which is solitary (kevala).
Again, this one beginning with the bow (cāpādima) should be given, situated in fire (vahnistha) and adorned by the womb (yonibhūṣita).
Varuṇa (va), endowed with three vowels (trisvaropeta), should follow, situated therein and again at its end.
Gaṇeśa, conjoined with fire (Ra), with his head pressed by the goad (U);
then pure nectar (Sa) again, marked with the three vowels (Ā, I, U);
again Gaṇendra (Ga) situated in fire (Ra), and then the moon (Sa) alone.
One should extract the prohibition [the letter *m*] traversed by three vowels, Soma situated with Varuṇa [the letter *v*],
the great fire [the letter *r*] marked with three dots, and Kālādya situated with Aśva [the letter *s*];
then Rudra preceded by Kālādya [the letter *y*]— thus one should extract them as a single cluster.
One should give Varuṇa alone, and Candra situated upon Varuṇa.
One should give the head of the eighth vowel alone, preceded by the Yoni;
then one should give Dvijihva alone, and again Niṣedha alone.
That very [seed-syllable], traversed by the three vowels, should again be given as the "double-tongued" (dvijihvaka).
It is the Lord of Elephants (gajanātha) together with the goad (sāṅkuśa), situated in Time (kālastha), joined with the fifth [vowel] and so forth.
Preceded by the Yoni, it is the Yoni-pattern (yonicitra), consisting of Nāda and Vahni joined with the sixth [vowel].
Endowed with the fourteenth vowel, its head struck by the bindu;
accompanied by the haṃsa and the visarga, O Goddess, then again the Krodha.
Then one should give the radiant [letter] joined with the *marmayonis* and the *nāyu*.
Again, one should extract the wind (*samīraṇa*) alone from the sixth and so forth;
then the fire (*vahni*), which is the first of the five, again located in the fifth and joined with the *visarga*.
The twenty-second word consists of seventy-four syllables;
it is proclaimed as the great mantra of the Goddess, fierce and incomparable.
It subdues great fear and destroys all calamities.
It destroys malevolent spells (*kṛtyā*) and the *khārkhoda* rite, and it rises against suffering and misfortune.
It is the peerless King of Mantras, causing fear to the *nāgas* and *asuras*.
When recited while situated in the *puruṣacakra*, it proceeds by means of the *tripurākrama*.
Then, O Goddess, it should be known as bestowing success during a great penance of a hundred repetitions. Whatever accomplishments (siddhis) are proclaimed in the Tantra for you,
O Queen of the Gods, he certainly achieves them all, O Goddess, by merely wearing the sandals.
Having again extracted the *tāraka* (the syllable Om), [place] the first of the winds (*vāyu*) alone;
then the *mahānāda* joined with *nāda*, the first of time (*kāla*) endowed with the eighth vowel;
then the seed-syllable of fire (*kṛśānu*) alone should be given, followed by Varuṇa adorned with the womb (*yoni*).
That which stands upon Varuṇa (va) and ends with him (ta), with Vahni (ra) as its crest-jewel over three vowels (i);
Varuṇa (va) inlaid with that (ra), ending with Kuṇḍala (la) and joined with the fifth (e);
again, Śakra (ka) situated between Vahni (ra) and Kāla (ma), conjoined with Mohana (na).
One should extract the arm situated there, preceded by the womb (yoni) located in the fifth [position].
This foot should be made twofold; O Goddess, one should utter the sound (nāda) twice.
Adorned with the great womb (mahāyoni), it is the first of the sixth, situated in fire (vahni).
One should extract the beautiful [seed-syllable] marked with a goad, upon which a horse is mounted by its head,
and which is adorned on the crown by a dot and accompanied by a goad.
The *nāda* is the head of the three vowels; it should be applied in two ways as the supreme syllable.
The skull (*kharpara*) should be placed sevenfold, wherein the first triad belongs to fire (*vahni*).
Another triad, with the *bindu* as its head and belonging to the fire of time (*kālāgni*), is also to be placed there.
One should again give three others joined with the *bindu* and the *praṇava*.
This supreme *pada* is to be known as fourfold in its entirety.
And the fifth is the *nāda*, adorned with the three vowels and conjoined with the *aṅkuśa*.

This word is to be divided into two parts: "Varuṇa" marked with three vowels, and the third part beginning with the first [consonant], which has the form of a mass (piṇḍa) situated in the womb (yoni). After that comes the "wrath of the Goddess" (devīkrodha), followed by the "Sound" (nāda) endowed with emanation (sṛṣṭi).
This twenty-third word is remembered as consisting of fifty syllables.
By means of this king of words, one should perform initiation in all its forms:
initiation into the principles (tattva-dīkṣā), initiation into the cosmic powers (kalā-dīkṣā), initiation into the worlds (bhauvanī), and initiation by the contraction of the words (pada-saṃkṣepaka).
Initiation by color (varṇadīkṣā), initiation by mantra (mantradīkṣā), and likewise initiation by power (śaktidīkṣā);
initiation by life-force (jīvadīkṣā), initiation by recitation (vāradīkṣā), and likewise initiation by touch (sparśadīkṣā);
initiation by piercing (vedhadīkṣā) is known as the sixfold [initiation], and initiation by speech (vāgdīkṣā) is remembered as another.
The initiation of the jar (ghaṭadīkṣā), the initiation of the cloth (paṭadīkṣā), and another initiation of the jar;
another which bestows immediate liberation (sadyonirvāṇadā), and likewise that which is called nirvāṇikī;
another known as the half-moon restraint (ardhacandranirodhā), and the supreme one remembered as the movement of sound (nādacārā).
There may be another initiation called Vyāpinī, and another known as Samanā;
likewise, there is the initiation named Unmanā, and another designated as Guruvaktra.

The initiation called *ajā*, or that which consists of the objects of touch, as well as that called *praśāntā*; the supreme initiation of emission (*visarga*), the most excellent of the excellent initiations of the fixed point (*dhruva*);
and the initiation of light (*āloka*), O Subhagā, which is other [than those] and arises from knowledge and realization (*jñāna-vijñāna*).
Of the forty-three initiations that have been proclaimed,
the Guru should perform all of them effortlessly in the midst of the King of Padas.
This Pada, O Great Lord, should be known as bestowing liberation through its recitation.
For one who recites with deceit, success remains far away.
Having extracted [the mantra] beginning with Gaṇeśa and ending with Mahākuṇḍalībandha,
it is adorned with the Yoni-bindu mounted upon the back of the god's face.
This is declared to be the *piṇḍa*, which grants the accomplishment of immediate union.
Having extracted Kālāgnirudra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, and Śakra,
as well as Kāla and Ananta, one should likewise extract Vahni and Nāda.
The half-moon, the bindu, and the supreme śāntakalā—
this is the piṇḍa, formed as a single mass, the foremost leader of all mantras. If one recites it correctly, it brings about possession in an instant.
Bhairava, encased by fire and marked with the Mohanī and the Bindu;
when Śiva is to be given again, one should extract the Earring situated in fire, conjoined with the Yoni and the Bindu, as the pure Kāla.
The *nāda* joined with *nāda*, and the third [letter] alone;
again, situated at the vital point of the horse (*aśvamarmasthita*), preceded by the *yoni* and accompanied by the goad (*sāṅkuśa*).
Śakra with the three vowels on its head, preceded by the *yoni*, and the *la* with the goad.
Having extracted only Śakra, one should extract the goad and fire;
[the letter] at the beginning of the fifth, situated in fire, struck on the head by three suns.
One should give only the "double-tongued" (dvijihva) [letter], with time (kāla) established as the flavor (svādima).
Having extracted only the wind (vāyu), make this position twofold.
Then, having extracted fire (vahni) along with the goad (sāṅkuśa), [place] only Varuṇa thereafter.
Having again bestowed the wind [seed-syllable], fashion this word in the following manner:
place the water [syllable] *āṃ* as it is pervaded by the three vowels (*ā-i-u*), preceded by the bow (*ha*) and situated upon fire (*ra*).
One should form this with the goad (*sa*) and then extract Varuṇa (*va*).
Again, having extracted the letter *vāyu* (ya), form this word in two parts. The letter *varuṇa* (va) alone is to be given, followed by *candra* (u) adorned with three vowels (*ī*).
Then *amṛta* (a) and so forth, situated upon *sūrya* (r); then *ṣaṣṭha* (ṣa) and so forth, resting upon *vahni* (ra).

Having fashioned [the maṇḍala] adorned with three suns, variegated with the womb (yoni), and provided with the wind [vowels], make the syllable *jhāṃ* situated at the beginning of the vowels, accompanied by Rudra and Kāla. Then, place the first of the five [consonants] in the fifth position, doubled, and joined with the *nāda* and *visarga*.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, one should again utter the *nāda* (the nasal sound) joined with *nāda*, giving it twice.
One should extract the fire (*ra*) preceded by the *yoni* (the letter *ī*) and joined with *nāda*, also twice.
One should give the water-god (*va*) together with the goad (*ha*), preceded by the *yoni* and joined with the fifth vowel (*u*).
One should extract Śakra (Ś) joined with the womb-vowel (Ī), followed by Kāla (K) and the rest, enveloped by Mohanā (Ū).
Then one should extract Amṛta (A) and the rest in their entirety, and Vāyu (Y) alone.
One should extract Varuṇa (V) endowed with three vowels, situated therein, and its final part.
The sixth [vowel] with its initial [consonant] should be joined with a bindu and struck by an ankusha;
one should extract the fifth [vowel] with its initial [consonant] as it stands alone, and the wind [ha] alone.
The bow [jha] with its initial [consonant] is pervaded by the pranava [om], and the moon [sa] with its initial [consonant] is joined with a bindu.
Striking with the goad at the crown of the head, one should exhale only the *kāla* [vāyu];
and having restrained the fire within the bow and so forth, one should exhale only the *vāyu*.
The double-tongued [Sa] joined with Mohanī [Ū], Varuṇa [Va] situated upon a Bindu;
the Granthiśa [Ra] alone should be given, followed by that which is on the bow [Pha];
again Vāyu [Ya] alone, and the second [Pha] alone again.

Again, the negation (niṣedha) should be given, and that [should be] situated in the bow (cāpa) and so forth. Adorned with a triangle at its head, one should extract the Moon (sa) situated in Varuṇa (va),
joined with the "mouth-torn" (mukhadāraṇa), and combined with that, one should extract the Sound (nāda).
The Yoni-mantra should be preceded by the Sāṅkuśa; Vahni (Ra) should be adorned with the Yoni.
Varuṇa (Va) should be given alone, and then again Soma (Sa) alone.
Candra (Ca) should be placed at the beginning of the Yoni and provided with Mukhadāraṇa (Ha).
The fire [syllable] marked with *oṃ*, conjoined with *bhīma* (the letter *bha*) and *śaṅku* (*śa*), and obstructed by *nirodha* (*ra*);
the double-tongued [serpent] (*dvijihva*) joined with *mohana* (*na*), and Varuṇa (*va*) marked with *praṇava* (*oṃ*);
the fifth [vowel] (*ū*) at the beginning, situated within its own self (*svātman*), with its head pressed down by the goad (*aṅkuśa*).
Having extracted only the Fire (ra), what could one extract from the Wind (ya)?
O Maheśvarī, having joined the Sound (nāda) with the Resounding (nāda) and pierced it with the Bindu,
this word is proclaimed as the collection of the essence of all things.
It possesses eighty-one syllables and bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Just so, the twenty-fourth word should be recited;
it is known to cause agitation in all beings and to grant liberation through its mere remembrance.
In the three worlds, there is no action that cannot be accomplished by this;
O fortunate one, through a hundred repetitions of these words of the Great-Souled One,
knowledge shall manifest within his own continuum— of this there is no doubt.
Through mere recitation, he effects the divine purification of the five;
for one who dwells in the cremation ground, the perfection of the great assembly (*mahāmelāpa*) arises,
as well as the destruction of ghosts, *vetālas*, *khārkhodas*, *kṛtyās*, and *yasmās*.
The King of the Mantras should perform this repeatedly with a single sprinkling;
moreover, he should destroy the effects of rams, winds, and thunderbolts merely by recollecting [the mantra].
By the mere recollection [of this], one shall destroy the defects arising from royal oppression, those born of fate, and all internal defects; indeed, for the practitioner,
the immobilization of an army occurs through mere recitation.

By means of the worship of this *pada*, the mantra-practitioner effortlessly performs subjugation, attraction, inciting enmity, killing, and expulsion, among other rites. One should perform all the initiations previously mentioned by means of this very [mantra].
O Goddess of the gods, this state of yours, which is equal to a wish-fulfilling gem and for which no equal exists, has been proclaimed by me.
Furthermore, Mahāmāyā, Kāla, and Kevala are to be bestowed again.

O Supreme Goddess, one should fashion the *kṛṣāṇḍa* adorned with three vowels, joined with *nāda*, joined with *nādasamāyukta*, and likewise with *antaka*; one should fashion *rāvaṇa* situated in fire (*vahni*), adorned with the *yoni* and the *bindu*.
The syllable *haṃsa* ending with the *kuṇḍala* (the bindu), mounted on fire (*ra*), followed again by *kāla* (the letter *ka*) standing [there],
then again *kāla* accompanied by the goad (*śa*), and fire (*ra*) adorned with the three vowels (*ai*).
This pair of words is declared to be most terrible and difficult to overcome.
The twenty-fifth, consisting of five syllables, is declared to be the supreme word;
and the twenty-sixth, O Goddess of Gods, is the cause of the destruction of the three worlds.
By the mere remembrance of these two kings of words, this entire universe, both moving and unmoving, [is sustained].
They certainly cause the descent of the Viṣṇu-purāṇa;
then, having again extracted the double-tongued [serpent], marked with the *mohana*-bindu,
and having placed it upon fire, preceded by the *yoni* and accompanied by the goad (*aṅkuśa*).
Having extracted Śakra alone, one should extract the fire [letter] together with the goad [vowel].
Make the first letter of the fifth [group] mounted upon the fire [letter] and adorned with three vowels.
Furthermore, it should be given preceded by the *yoni*, with its head stepped upon by the *aṅkuśa*.
Having extracted *Śakra* alone, one should extract *Soma* alone.
O Dear One, that which ends in *gha* should be placed at the beginning of the *yoni*, and that which begins with *amṛta* [should be placed] there.
One should again extract the horse, the three-syllabled one, and the head;
then the crow together with the goad, O Supreme Goddess, and Indra alone.
Then the vulva-design, Mahākāla, and the double-tongued one alone.
One should extract the syllable *kāla* (ka) mounted upon *kāla* (ka), followed by the negation (*niṣedha*) marked with three vowels (*trisvara*).
Then one should again extract the *praṇava* (*oṃ*) of *kāla* (ka), followed by *nāda* alone.
Then the horse (*aśva*) alone at the head, and again *kāla* (ka) at the beginning alone.
Again, one should place *kāla* (the letter *ka*) situated at the beginning, its head (*mastaka*) traversed by *praṇava* (the syllable *oṃ*);
then the first of the fifth [group] (*pa*), together with the arrow and bow (*saśaracāpa*) and adorned with the *yoni*.
Again, O Goddess, one should give *kāla*, accompanied by *nāda* and joined with *nāda*.
Then, O Goddess, one should extract Śakra ending with Kuṇḍalī, whose crest is adorned by the Yoni, joined with the Praṇava; then Vāyu joined with the Yoni, ending with Varuṇa, and situated therein.
Then Gaṇeśa joined with the Yoni, ending with Varuṇa, and likewise situated there.
One should utter the fire (Ra) marked with three dots (Bindu), then the skull-bowl (Kha), and again the fire (Ra).
This is conjoined with the Sound (Nāda) and the extinction of fire (Kṣaya), preceded by Sāma and marked with the three vowels.
Then one should utter Kekara, Yoni, Mūrdhāna, Bhairava, and finally Kevala.
Having extracted that which is mounted upon it, together with the three vowels and the horse-mark,
one should again provide the end of the *puṣkala*, and again provide it marked with a half-syllable.
The arm situated in the fifth [position] is pierced by the head of three dots;
the first of the bows is conjoined with fire, and fire is joined with the goad.
Then there is the double-tongued one, whose head is the womb and which is situated upon Varuṇa at its beginning.

The fire-syllable (ra) adorned with three dots (bindus), preceded by the yoni (ī); then the fire-syllable alone; having extracted the fire-syllable alone, it is placed at the end of the letter *gha* (ghaṃ) and preceded by the yoni (ī). Then the letter *ka* (kāla) joined with the fifth vowel (u), followed by the skull-syllable (kha) struck by the three vowels (ai).
Having extracted the *nāda* alone, [place] the Moon situated in its own self;
then the Visarga alone should be given, and then Śakra situated in the sixth.
[Place] that which begins with Soma, traversed by the three vowels, and that which begins with Kāla, joined with the eighth.
Having extracted only the Fire (Ra), then the Yoni-mark (E), and then Varuṇa (Va);
one should place that first letter situated therein, marked with three dots (the Aṇḍaka).
Then the Earring (Sa), presided over by the three vowels (Ā, I, U), preceded by the Yoni (E), and ending with Svā.
The head [of the horse] is struck by a goad, adorned with the three vowels;
marked by that [goad], the horse is further [joined] with a bow adorned with the three vowels.
[The syllable] beginning with *amṛta* (a) is situated upon a crow, resting on the seventh vowel.

One should extract the Fire (Ra) conjoined with the Elephant-Goad (U), followed by Jihvīla (Ū) struck by the Yoni (M); then Varuṇa (Va) at the end of that, and having combined them into a single cluster,
one should extract the Fire (Ra) joined with the three vowels (Ā, I, U), and finally extract Nāda alone.
One should place the Moon within oneself;
then, having extracted the Fire situated in the sixth position, which consists of three vowels and is the sacrifice of the Kalās,
one should again place the Sun alone, with the Fire as its head and the Aṅkuśa above it.
(134a) Then,
the moon is variegated with the womb-syllables and remains ending with Varuṇa;
it is joined with the three bindus, and the fire-syllable is likewise joined with the moon alone.
One should contemplate Fire (Ra) constricted by Varuṇa (Va), with its head marked by the Praṇava (Oṃ);
then the first of the fifth [group] (Ū) situated within one's own body; then Time (Ma) adorned by the seventh (Sa).
Again, Time (Ma) alone, then Nāda, and again Nāda struck by Nāda.
Again, one should take the syllable struck by *punar* (the letter *na*), the wind (*sa*) marked with the seventh vowel (*ū*),
that which is joined with the splitting of the mouth (*ha*), the Lord of the Gaṇas belonging to Varuṇa (*va*),
with its head occupied by the seventh vowel (*ū*), and ending with Varuṇa (*va*) situated therein.
Adorned with three vowels, the arm is beautified by the syllable *vā* [of Varuṇa].
Place *varuṇa* at the end of that, and on one side place the *aṅkuśa*. Preceded by the *yoni*, it is the solitary *kevalin*, the *kṛṣāṇḍa* which reaches the beginning of immortality (*amṛta*).

The horse (ha) joined with the three vowels (i, ī, u), conjoined with Vāruṇa (va); one should extract Varuṇa (va) and that which ends with it (the anusvāra) as a single cluster. Again, place Vahni (ra) in the sixth position, preceded by the sixth vowel (ū) and endowed with the three vowels (i, ī, u).
The letter *ha* marked [by *ya*], the *haṃsa* situated in the fifth [vowel],
the horse (*a*) situated at the vital point (*marmasthita*), and again the end-maker (*kṣa*) situated in the fifth [vowel];
the *kharpara* (*ra*) traversed by three vowels, and the moon (*u*) adorned with the *praṇava*.
Having extracted only the *paśu*, as well as the fire (*anala*) with the goad (*sāṅkuśa*),
the double-tongued one (*dvijihva*) pierced by the womb (*yonisaṃbhinna*), and that which stands at the end of Varuṇa;
[and] the fire whose head consists of three vowels, and that which begins with the third [vowel] with the goad.
One should extract the horse situated at the vital point, mounted on the fifth *kṛtānta* (the letter *ṣa*),
joined with the great *yoni* (the vowel *e*) and the first of the third [group] (the letter *ga*), conjoined with three *bindus*.
One should extract the letter of negation (ṅ) situated in the fifth [vowel] and joined with *mukhadāraṇā* (the letter ṛ);
then again, O Goddess of Gods, the letter at the end (kṣ), followed by the horse (e) situated in the third vowel (i).
One should extract the letter preceded by *yonipūrva* (the letter ṇ) joined with *mukhadāraṇā* (the letter ṛ).
One should extract the "Prohibitor" (niṣedha) which is joined with the "Indra-hook" (indra-aṅkuśa) and begins with the letter *ya*.
Then, one should again extract its first letter, preceded by the "Yoni" (yonipūrva), situated in the seventh position;
this Prohibitor should be extracted conjoined with the three vowels.
One should extract the syllable Śakra alone, preceded by Yoni and situated in the fifth position;
it is struck by Aṅkuśa, joined with Bāhu, adorned with Dvijihva,
and Yoni, ending with Varuṇa, remaining in that state, possessing the face of a deity, and struck by the three vowels.
Then, one should again provide the double-tongued [Sa], overcome by delusion [Na], and Varuṇa [Va] alone.

Next, the first of the third [group] [Ta] should be given, preceded by the womb [E] and residing in its own body [A]. Then, it should be encased between the womb [E] and fire [Ra], ending with Varuṇa [Va] and beginning with that [E].
One should extract the Fire (Ra) conjoined with the three vowels (Ā, Ī, Ū), then the Water (Va) pierced by that [Fire],
then the end of Varuṇa (La) situated at the beginning of that [Water], and finally the pure Śakra (Sa).
Make Ananta (Ha) constricted by Kāla (Kṣa) and adorned with the three vowels.
One should place Varuṇa together with him [the preceding letter], and then the first Varuṇa;
ending with Varuṇa, it is solitary, preceded by the womb (Yoni), and joined with three Suns.
That which stands at the beginning of the fifth should be made, starting from the third, joined with three Suns.
One should extract the first of the fifth [vowel] and the first of the sixth [vowel], and the fire [letter], into one place;
preceded by the womb [letter], it stands in the seventh position, joined with the first of the fifth [vowel] and three suns [the letter *ra*].

The Mahānāda mantra consists of four parts; therein, the first two should be joined with the Visarga, and the other two should be joined with the Unmanī, O Maheśvarī. Soma is conjoined with Varuṇa and joined with Mukhadāraṇā.
The sound (nāda) joined with ten thousand sounds should be made; it is the most supreme of the supreme words.
It should be known as the twenty-seventh [chapter], which bestows all prosperity. This excellent collection consists of one hundred and seventy-one syllables.
It should be known as the bestower of all happiness and is remembered as the giver of fearlessness in all circumstances;
it destroys the fault of all intermixture and annihilates all obstacles.
O Goddess of the Gods, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished by this.
It should be known as the performer of all rites even for a practitioner through mere remembrance.
O fortunate one, by reciting it but once, it bestows fortune and liberation upon men;
at the time of death, whoever looks upon this [mantra] and recites it [attains the goal].
The practitioner shall lead him to union with Brahman; of this there is no doubt.
O Bhairavī, by the mere remembrance of this, one is seen directly like Bhairava himself.
In whatever place one recites this unsurpassed king of words, [there he shall attain success].

O Goddess, by the power of the Thousand-fold Command through yoga, he leads that entire region, together with all things mobile and immobile, to union with Śiva. O Goddess, the Great Convergence (mahāmelāpaka) occurs simply through remembrance.
This state consists of all goddesses and consists of all Rudras;
it is the performer of all protection and is intent upon devouring the three worlds.
Whether it be for pacification (śāntika) or nourishment (pauṣṭika), this increases longevity and health.

In whichever wheel or support (ādhāra) one recites [the mantra] while worshipping the deity, that [wheel or support] should be known as the bestower of success in that [rite]. What is the use of saying more?
In whatever way it may be designated, it should be known as the warder-off of all calamities,
the bestower of all prosperity, and that which grants success through constant recitation. Once this king of words has been attained, from that moment forth, the practitioner—
It is understood that just as Bhairavanāyaka is [worshipped] in the Śaktikula,
so too in all the Tantras, whatever is investigated regarding ritual action and practice,
one should accomplish it according to all those doctrines through recollection alone.
Then, one should extract the most terrible and wonderful Krodha in two parts:
having extracted Kālakevala from the fifth [letter] as the first, along with the eighth;
and one should likewise extract Varuṇa at its end, dividing it into two parts.
O Goddess of the gods, one should then extract the fire (Ra) like a single syllable (*piṇḍa*);
it should be adorned with the three vowels (*e*, *ai*, *au*) and followed by the sixth vowel (*ū*), thus forming *Rū*.
Having extracted the fire alone, one should likewise extract the end-syllable (*Ha*).
The letter *va* (the third consonant) split by three dots (*bindu*), situated within one's own body; its head adorned with the *yoni* (the vowel *ī*), and the moon (*ca*) resting upon that *varuṇa*;
joined with the "mouth-torn" (*mukhadāraṇa*, the vowel *e*), and then the *nāda* struck by *nāda*.
This twenty-eighth pada consists of thirteen syllables;
it destroys the faults of the great samaya and annihilates the most heinous sins.
Having become the body of the Avadhūta, the practitioner is indeed beyond conventional conduct.
(136a) One should recite this with mindfulness, free from pride;
being purified by the five jewels and well-sealed with the five mudrās.
Through the grace of the Goddess Maheśvarī, one attains the perfection of the union (*melāpa*).
Then, having extracted the Savior (*tāraka*), which consists of the fifth [vowel] with the first [consonant], together with the seventh;
the third with the first, which is solitary (*kevalin*); and the womb (*yoni*) with the first, established with its limbs (*aṅga*).
One should give only the tongue (jihvīla), which is the first [letter] situated as fire (va).
Having extracted the negation (niṣedha) in two ways, the last [part] is struck by the three vowels (trisvara).
One should give only the letter ṣa, which is the first of the third [group], together with Caṇḍa.
First, one should extract the fire situated within one's own body, pierced by the goad;
then, having extracted the fire alone, one should extract the bow from the beginning of the mouth.
One should extract the bow alone, its tip struck by the goad.

One should extract the fire (ra) conjoined with its own destruction (ha), [the letter] at the mouth of the well (kha) together with fire (ra), and likewise the head of Mohanī (i) with a bindu; one should extract the end of that (na) in the same way.
Then, having extracted the bow (ca) in that same manner, one should give back everything that preceded it.
The first of the sixth [group] alone, and again the immortal fire;
the fifth situated in the fifth—this word is thus extracted.
It should be known as the twenty-ninth, which brings about the full weight of all enjoyments.
O fair-browed one, this twenty-two-syllable mantra is thus known according to its true meaning.
By practicing it for seven days with this Lord of the Foot,
there is the expansion of all supports and the piercing of all cakras.
Furthermore, an incomparable and great pervasiveness arises for the practitioner;
there is nothing whatsoever in the world that cannot be accomplished by this.
Therefore, having made a firm resolve within himself, the practitioner of mantra should recite it.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, the *tāraka* (savior) mantra is again threefold, accompanied by the object of knowledge (*prameya*).
It begins with *kāla* (the letter *ka*), is established in *vahni* (the letter *ra*), and is encapsulated by the nasal dot (*bindu*) as its sixth element.

O Goddess, one should extract it three times; likewise, one should extract the double-tongued [S]. The sound (N) should be struck by the sound (N), and the great-powerful [M] should be divided by the bindu.
This indeed consists of thirty [units], a ten-syllabled phrase of supreme excellence.
O Goddess, this supreme state bestows the attainment of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Chanted upon the *kaṃda*, the *syanda*, and likewise the *vidyā*, it grants success in all things;
it is declared to be the very essence of the entire seat of knowledge (*vidyāpīṭha*).
O Goddess of gods, there is nothing that this king of mantras cannot accomplish most effectively.
Furthermore, O beloved, having extracted the *kuṇḍala* and encased it with fire (*vahni*),
marked at the head with the *yoni* and the *bindu*, this is the *piṇḍa* of great power.
Make the "double-tongued" (dvijihva), seated upon Bhairava, encapsulated by fire (vahni).
This is the "body" (piṇḍa) endowed with the "deluder" (mohanī) and the bindu, which possesses great power.
One should employ the "double-tongued," mounted on the fifth [vowel], and pierced by the bindu.

The supreme five-syllable mantra, formed by adding the Moon (ca) to the creation-mantra (sa), should be joined with the Praṇava (oṃ) at its end; it is pleasing, bestows all desires, and wards off all ailments.
It should be known as the thirty-first [mantra], the destroyer of all misfortune.
It should be known that when there is intense devotion toward the root [mantra], it bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
when recited by a preeminent practitioner, it grants the attainment of happiness and good fortune.
This unsurpassed state is obtained when received from the mouth of the Guru.
At that very moment, the liberation of that practitioner is proclaimed;
O Goddess, this state has been declared by me to you as "Mṛtyuñjaya" (the Conqueror of Death). (137a)

O Bhairavī, beloved of those who bow before you, this [practice] which perfectly brings about peace and nourishment occurs even for one on the verge of death through the mere remembrance of the Great Melāpa; and the Yoginīs always bestow what is beneficial upon him.
O Goddess, one should cause that supreme king of words, which resides within the heart, to be bestowed—
having again extracted the *tāraka* and likewise the *niṣedha*,
joined with the *praṇava*, and ending with *kṛtānta*.
One should extract Kṛtānta alone, then Nāda together with Nāda; again, Kāla joined with Nāda, the fifth letter together with the seventh;
Kālādi occupied by the eighth, and Vahni alone.
One should extract Varuṇa marked with the Yoni and situated within Varuṇa as the last [letter];
likewise, one should extract Vahni marked with three vowels, and Yama alone.
One should make the Nāda endowed with Nāda, and extract Vahni from the beginning of the sixth.
One should place the letter *ka* alone, followed by *pu*, *ru*, *ṣa*, and *ca*, joined with *pa*, *ma*, *ṅku*, and *śa*.
One should place *kā* and *la* in the *niṣedha* (the second cell), joined with *saṃ* and *ruḍha*, and accompanied by *mu*, *kha*, *dā*, and *raṇa*.
One should place *va* and *ru* alone, and form [the word] situated between *so* and *māṃ*.
It should be adorned with three vowels, beginning with the fifth [consonant], and accompanied by its source (the *yonimudrā*).
This word is exceedingly fierce, inspiring fear even in fear itself.
Consisting of twenty-one syllables, this king of words bestows all accomplishments (*siddhi*).
O highly fortunate one, the thirty-second [chapter] reveals the splendor of the Supreme Radiance.
One should thus recite this mantra within the Bindu-pitcher, which manifests the form of the Goddess;
it is the essence that bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, granting salvation from the three worlds.
O Goddess, when this has been attained, it should be understood that my powers are fully engaged.
As taught by the Lord Bhairava, this is declared to be the recollection that bestows accomplishment.
O Goddess, one should accomplish what has been recited according to the desire of the practitioner.

Again, having extracted [the syllable] ending in the vital point (*marman*), adorned with fire (*ra*) and the *nāda*, and joined with the *bindu*— O Goddess, this is the wrath of the Goddess (*devyākrodha*) repeated three times, and again twice.
The first [syllable] should be with the *nāda* and preceded by the womb (*yoni*), beautified by that very *vāhna*.
Then the negation (*niṣedha*) situated at the beginning of the fifth, followed again by the primordial deity (*devādya*) alone.
The letter of Varuṇa should be given with the *nāda*, and the moon (*candra*) beautified by three vowels.
Then, together with that negation (niṣedha), there is the solitary Puruṣa;
then the Nāda joined with Nāda, and again the Moon situated in the mud and so forth;
mounted upon the letter *ra*, it becomes the condensed *piṇḍa*, pierced by the goad (*aṅkuśa*) of Vahni.
Make the double-tongued [ha] together with the womb [e], and place the two nasals [ṅa-ṅaḥ] situated within the *piṇḍa*.
The fire [ra] joined with three suns [o], the double-tongued [ha] accompanied by delusion [i],
Varuṇa [va], and the third vowel [u] at the beginning— these are the individual leaders of the syllables.
The first [syllable] is the Yoni (V), joined with the Piṇḍa (AU) and adorned with the Fire-Yoni (R).
At the end of "Ī" and "AṂ", the two Piṇḍas (AU and AU) should be given; this is the face of the deity, accompanied by the three dots (M).
It is endowed with the Nāda (H) and that which is equal to the Nāda (S), with its head beautified by the Bindu (M).
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, the Great Nectar joined with Creation should be given in two ways.
This thirty-third word consists of twenty-eight syllables.
There is nothing in this world that one cannot accomplish by means of it.
It purifies the seven sins, including the destruction of the *liṅga* and so forth.
O Goddess, this state which bestows liberation through recitation has been declared by me.
O Goddess, it should be uttered with the application of *kumbhaka* (breath-retention) even when one is angry.
Having joined the name of the enemy with the [mantra] syllables, slay him;
by one hundred recitations, he slays even the great son of Śakra.
Or, O Goddess, one should meditate through the yoga of dhyāna upon her who resembles the fire of cosmic destruction,
cutting that victim with a sword, his eyes wide with terror.
Then, O Goddess, she of great strength, dark as the throat of a peacock, laughs aloud.
This state bestows all desires—[it is] that very [state].
Furthermore, the "language of the crow" (kākabhāṣā) should be given; one should extract only the word of Śakra (Indra).
Mahākāla, situated in the fifth position, is the skull-bowl adorned by the corner.

Furthermore, the "Crow Language" (kākabhāṣā) should be given: one should extract the letter *kraṃ* together with the *yoni*, and then lift up *varuṇa* and *caṇḍanātha* as a single compound (*piṇḍībhūta*). One should give the arm adorned with three dots (*tribindu*) as the "Crow Language" once again.
Furthermore, one should bestow Indra; Varuṇa marked with three vowels;
Kṛtānta accompanied by the Praṇava;
and the solitary Niṣedha, beginning with the third [vowel], marked with three vowels.
The syllable *bā* followed by the third vowel (*u*), joined with the second [consonant] (*kha*);
then the first of the bow-syllables (*ca*) accompanied by fire (*ra*), and again the first of the bow-syllables (*ca*) alone;
then the wind-syllable (*ya*) topped with the third vowel (*ū*), and the fifth [consonant] (*pa*) joined with the source (*ma*).
One should extract only the arm, and again the horse situated at the vital point;
then one should extract the man mounted on the fifth [horse],
and indeed again the great-sounding one mounted by Rudra at the beginning of the edge.
Furthermore, the "Crow Language" (kākabhāṣā) should be given, adorned with three vowels for Śakra;
O Maheśānī, Mahāmāyā, joined with Nāda and Fire (R), should be made conjoined with Sṛṣṭi (H);
then the Goddess should give Krodha (K).
The thirty-fourth should be known as the supreme syllable consisting of thirty letters.
When it has ascended to the navel-center, it hangs down like the supreme dancer.
O Goddess, when this word has passed away, it then becomes manifest. O Goddess, when one recites this word while it is situated within the belly of the vibration (*spanda*),
then, O Goddess, one understands the time that is passing away.
When one utters this word mounted upon the *bindu-kalā*,
then, remaining unwearied, one knows everything pertaining to the three periods of time.
Through recollection, one sees in a dream all that which is desired.

Prasenā accomplishes the *khorikā* that revolves everywhere in an instant. By mere play, the practitioner indeed effects the possession (*āveśa*) by arrows, the possession by creepers, the supreme possession by the mace, and the possession by the sword.
O Goddess of the gods, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished by means of this [mantra] word.
Again, having extracted the *tāraka* (the syllable Om), one should extract the fire-syllable (*ra*) from the sixth [position].
Then [one should take] the Puruṣa, the Yoni, the Head, Delusion, and likewise Wrath.
This five-syllabled word is indeed the thirty-fifth word.
O highly fortunate goddess, this word bestows sovereignty over the three worlds; established in the heart-lotus, it accomplishes whatever is desired by the mind.

Furthermore, the first of all should be given: the trident (Śūla) conjoined with the Praṇava (Oṃ), followed by Vahni (Ra), Tatkṣaya (Ū), and Mahākrodha (Hūṃ). This four-syllabled [mantra] is indeed the thirty-sixth supreme pada.

It bestows all accomplishments, is the essence, and causes immediate immersion; it pierces all knots instantly by means of a single word. One shall attain one's own supreme nature, which is the state of true illumination.
The accomplishment beginning with *parāparā* shall be established through the moments and locations;
having extracted the first of the sixth [group] again, one should extract the solitary fire (*vahni*).

The syllable *puruṣa* alone is to be given, joined with the *śūla* (the *kṣa*) and the *praṇava* (*oṃ*). The *bāhu* (the *na*) should be made joined with the *yoni* (*ī*), and the *nāda* (*ha*) accompanied by *sṛṣṭi* (*e*).
This six-syllabled word is remembered as the thirty-seventh.

It is declared to be the remover of all sins and the consumer of the faults of the great commitments (mahāsamaya). O Bhairavī, whatever sin has been accumulated by men through their births and so forth, it is reduced to ashes merely by the remembrance of this [mantra].
Moving [the tongue] once upon the tip of the tongue destroys all sin;
it bestows great liberation and the eight supernatural powers (siddhis).
That which resides within the cavity of the *laṃbikā* accomplishes every goal.
Furthermore, O Goddess, one should extract this first syllable situated between Tejasvin and Varuṇa;
its head marked by the Praṇava, then again the bow alone,
and finally the arms with their heads traversed by the three vowels.
Furthermore, O Goddess worshipped by the gods, having extracted the syllable *krodha*,
this five-syllabled word is indeed the thirty-eighth, O Beloved;
it is known as the supreme word that pervades the entire universe.
Even without being spoken to, the great mountain ranges tremble;
the celestial dwellers raise shouts of victory for the practitioner,
and the sky-faring goddesses, O best of gods, certainly worship him.
One should know that this bestows all siddhis and draws forth great blood;
by means of this word, one should accomplish the extraction of the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
By means of this king of words, one should accomplish all rites.
O Maheśvarī, the Great Sound (mahānāda) is to be given in three ways, distinguished by the bindu:
the first resides in the sound of fire (agnināda), and the second reaches the delusion of fire (vahnimoha).
O you who are worshipped by the best of gods, the third [letter] situated on the sixth fire (the letter *ṣ*) should be employed.
Amṛta (the letter *sa*) mounted on Varuṇa (the letter *va*), joined with Mukhadāraṇā (the letter *ra*),
and Nāda (the letter *ha*) struck by Nāda (the letter *ha*)— this five-syllabled word has been extracted.
The fortieth chapter, minus one, has been described to you in brief.
This state that bestows liberation has been described to you in summary.
By means of this sovereign state, he accomplishes the world of the moving and the unmoving.

This state, which brings about the great gathering, is remembered but once. O Mistress of the God of Gods, by the mere remembrance of the Triple Void, it effects piercing, striking, obstruction, and so forth, as well as an extensive possession.

O beautiful lady, it should be known that this brings about all actions merely by being remembered; this word is declared to be common to all tantras. Having extracted the syllable *kāla* alone, one should then place *nāda* and *nādahata*.
One should utter Kālādya (the letter *ka*) preceded by Gaṇeśa (*ga*), followed by Vāyu (*ya*) and Ādaga (*na*).
One should give Varuṇa (*va*) alone, and then extract Candra (*ca*) with the goad (*śa*).
Niṣedha (*ha*) is presided over by the three vowels (*ī*, *ai*, *au*), and Yonyādya (*la*) is adorned by the Yoni (*m*).
One should again bestow the beneficial [syllable] following the double-tongued [visarga] along with the *visarga*.
This supreme ten-syllabled (*daśārṇa*) word, the fortieth, should be known;
this word, worshipped by the best of gods, bestows enjoyments upon mere remembrance.
From the time that the supreme state was attained by the foremost of practitioners,
from that moment on, their prosperity shall extend for seven generations;
O Goddess, it shall be with the practitioner-lord just as it is with Nārāyaṇa.
The immovable syllable (A) invariably bestows prosperity and the abundance of wealth and grain.
Then, having extracted the *tāraka* (Om), one should again place the prohibitive syllable (M).
The wise man should apply the syllable of Time (KṢ) as it is pervaded by the *praṇava* (Om).
Then the "crow-language" (*kākabhāṣā*) should be given, adorned with the three tones of Śakra;
again, the "time" (*kāla*), the "kevalin," the "sound" (*nāda*), and that which is endowed with sound (*nādasamanvita*).
The "crow-language" (kākabhāṣā) should be given again, followed by Indra adorned with three ornaments.
Having extracted the sound alone, one should extract the fire alone.
Then the horse, conjoined with three vowels, and the bow consisting of the fifth bone.
One should extract Varuṇa mounted upon a skull, followed by Varuṇa alone;

then Kāla alone, followed by the negation (the letter *na*) struck by three vowels (*i*, *u*, *m*). Then the first [letter] of the third [group], which is solitary, together with the neighing of the horse's vital point (*aśvamarmasvanādaka*).
One should extract Śakra preceded by the womb (the letter *u*), adorned with three vowels.

Having raised the arm (the letter *ba*) along with the resonance (*nāda*), one should place Śakra, beautified by three vowels. Furthermore, the "crow-speech" (*kākabhāṣā*) should be given, beginning with the sixth [vowel] and joined with the resonance.
One should extract Indra, who has the three suns as his head, and with him the mark that is non-prohibitive.
Having extracted Indra alone, one should then draw Agni situated with Varuṇa;
after him, one should extract the double-tongued [serpent] marked by Varuṇa.

One should cause [the disciple] to receive [the mantra] whose head is pressed by the goad (aṅkuśa), which has the face of a deity, preceded by the womb (yonipūrva), beginning with nectar (amṛta), and accompanied by fire (savahnika). [Then] the horse (aśva) together with three dots (tribindu), ending with the earring (kuṇḍala), and accompanied by fire.
The *Haṃsa* (the letter *Ha*) mounted upon *Kāla* (the letter *Sa*), joined with the "mouth-torn" (*mukhadāraṇa*, the letter *Ra*);
the horse (*Aśva*, the letter *U*) joined with the goad (*Aṅkuśa*, the letter *U*), seated upon the Wind (*Samīraṇa*, the letter *Ya*). [This forms *Hūṃ*.
Then, the bow and so forth (*Cāpādyaṃ*), traversed by the three vowels (*Trisvara*, *Ā-I-U*), joined with *Kāla* (*Sa*) and the goad (*U*). [This forms *Sūṃ*.]
The first of the fifth [vowel] situated in the seventh [consonant] is a pure negation;
furthermore, that which is mounted on the beginning of the bow [the letter *ca*] is again a negation marked by three vowels.
Again, there is merely a prohibition, not situated upon a bow;
again, a mere prohibition joined with the splitting of the mouth;
again, that which is mounted on a bow and so forth, marked by knots, beginning with a bow, and further accompanied by a goad.
Having extracted the Wind (Y), marked with three suns (R) and a horse (H), and adorned by that very same [horse],
one should raise up Sadāśiva, who is the fivefold creator and consists of the five grains.
Then Mahāmāyāśvarī bestowed herself again as the fivefold [energy].
O Goddess, one should first extract Mahārāva, then Vahni adorned with Yoni and Bindu; these three should be drawn out, and thereafter one should take Candramas.
Then one should take the letter situated in Varuṇa along with Nāda, and again Nāda struck by Nāda.
O Goddess, this verse of yours, consisting of seventy syllables joined with forty [others], has been revealed; it bestows all prosperity,
pacifies all suffering, and destroys all harm.
It pacifies all misfortune and destroys fear and poverty. Whenever one remembers this word in the wheel of power (śakticakra) without distraction,
then that king of words shall accomplish all rites.
O King of Padas, O most excellent lady, whatever rites were previously prescribed for that other Jayadratha, all of those one should always perform here;
what is the use of further elaboration on this matter, O slender-waisted one?
Thus, O beloved, this most formidable Vidyā has been fully explained to you by me,
consisting of one thousand and sixty-four syllables;
and here, O lady of pure vows, there are forty Akīhikinis.
This most formidable vidyā is remembered as the performer of all rites.
However many king-tantras there may be situated within the Vidyāpīṭha,
such [a vidyā] is not found anywhere among those excellent king-tantras.

O Goddess of gods, O Maheśānī, I am not capable of explaining her vigor, her power, her manifestation, or the determination of her steps— even in ten million years— with tens of millions upon tens of millions of faces endowed with the state of Sadāśiva.
This is the supreme power, this is the supreme digit;
she is that Goddess Trīśvarī, she is the sovereign of the excellent wheel.
She resides at the end of the lineage of families; she is remembered as the forest of mantras. She is the sovereign of the wheel of earrings; she abides at the end of all weapons.
She is mounted upon the lineage of the channels (nāḍī); she is the one who restrains the neighing of horses.
She is that mistress of the navel-wheel, the serpent-like goddess longing for enjoyment;
she is mounted upon the family of karma, the supreme Aghora-vidyā;
she delights in the flowing belly, illuminating the triple consciousness.
O Mistress of the Kāli-kula, she is the one who differentiates the form of the jar;
she unfolds within the Ghaṇṭādhara of the Trivikrama-kula;
she possesses the splendor of the limbs of the intoxication of mantra, and is devoted to the lotus-forest of the bindu.
I have not remembered this internal flame (śikhā) of theirs as having ascended to a mere fraction [of its power].
The Supreme Goddess, the Mistress of Yoga, resides within the interior of the lotus of Śakti.
There is nothing that she does not create, and there is nothing that she does not accomplish.
There is no animal there, nor does the hand-bell of the God of gods burn;
yet from the mere utterance of her name, the universe, along with the Hūhukas,
trembles, shakes violently, and blazes up again and again.

He for whom the *prastāra* is cooked, as conceived by the mantra of the Goddess, becomes initiated in all *tantras*; of this there is no doubt. He becomes worthy of worship and honor by all those belonging to the *khecarīcakra*.
As long as one remembers this vidyā of terrible prowess for seven days,
so long does knowledge situated within one's own body arise for the practitioner;
O Goddess of gods, he is known intensely through his final birth.
O daughter of Tiri, this mantra of the Goddess is not obtained even in ten million eons.
This which I have told you is the most excellent of all, the most precious;
it is the most formidable Vidyā, the Supreme Ārkakālī, the thousand-syllabled Mistress of the Heart.
Or rather, what more shall I say? O Bhairavī, tell me quickly that which has come down through the lineage.
I shall tell you that secret, the supreme essence, the foremost, which is beneficial for your mind. (141b)

Thus, in the Bhairava-stream, in the Vidyāpīṭha, in the Śiraccheda, in the Jayadrathayāmala Mahātantra, in the twenty-four thousand [verse] work, in the third Ṣaṭka, in the Ghoraghoratara-cakra, this is the procedure for the extraction of the mantra of the Thousand-Syllabled [Goddess].
Having thus heard from the mouth of Bhairava, O Goddess of gods...
She became supremely delighted, filled with the nectar of contentment;
yet, falling once more into doubt, she spoke to the Lord of the Worlds. The Goddess said:

I am satiated, O Supreme Lord, by this great nectar of the scripture—this supreme, most wonderful secret that is to be drunk with the ears while being chewed [in the mind]. You are the Lord of all worlds; you are the Creator; you are the ultimate goal.
O destroyer of the enemy of wine (Śiva), you who are saluted by all the villages;

you are the great sun within the lotus of my heart, and you are the fierce flame moving through the *suṣumṇā* channel. You, as the moon of consciousness, shine forth upon the mountain ridges of the body.
You shine forth among the groves of the lotuses of awakening and as the sun;
you are the bearer of the digits of power and virility in the union of the three abodes.
You are the ornament of the foremost heroes upon the great cremation ground of the heart.
O Maheśvara, you are like a bee dwelling in the garden of the great and excellent karma, languid with intoxication;
you subsist on the nectar-juice of the *bindu*, and you are intensely attached to the lotus-foot.
O Lord, there is only one mistress for your feet, and no other.
Whether they are separate or not separate, or whether they are the solitary hero (ekavīra), she is to be worshipped as half of my own essential nature when not separate; thus, what is my doubt?
Bhairava said:
Excellent, you ask well, O Goddess, you who desire the welfare of the Lord of Elephants!
Although she is a Greatly Powerful One who is both a Solitary Heroine (Ekavīrā) and devoid of limbs (Niraṅgā),
nevertheless, listen to how Bhairavī is one and the same, despite being divided by name.
There is nothing whatsoever that differs in substance, though there is a difference in function and a difference in name.
Listen now to these [powers] which abide as the Mālinī-vidyā.
Huṃkāriṇī, Mahāmārī, Sthūlā, and likewise Aikatrā; another has her limbs smeared with cremation-ground ashes, while another has the three sacrificial fires in her heart;
she should be meditated upon as Citijvālākulā, and another as Śmaśānāsavā.
She who dwells in the great cremation ground, the beloved of the fire of time;
likewise Kaṣakarankī, Haṃṭāhaṭā, and Yudhānaṣā;
she who destroys all suffering and likewise the destroyer of deformity.
Mahābhīmā, Bhīṣaṇī, and Jvālāmālinī;
another is Sarvabhogapradā, and likewise Tṛptajvālā;
then Tridhāmāntaracāriṇī and Mahāḍambaranāśinī.
Likewise, Mokṣalakṣmī, and another, Daśanāṃtrikā in a secluded place;
Sarvānyā Mārikā, and another is remembered as Karālī; then Smṛtivināśā, and another, Paramāmṛtakarṣaṇī.
Likewise, there is Aparā, Kalāvāsā, and another, Jīvādhyāyinikā; likewise the goddess Mahāvidyā, as well as Mahāśāṅkāriṇī;
and she named Mahārāviṇī, as well as Śakunī and Caṅkurī.
