O Ādinātha, I now desire to hear about that supreme sovereign of tantras, the entirety of knowledge: how is it that she, the supreme goddess,
the mistress of mantras, the mantra-lady, the emaciated one, and the sovereign of the lords of the Siddhas?
She who bestows success, prosperity, and liberation, and destroys sin—
beginning with Rambhā, she consists of up to one thousand syllables, or as few as seventeen.
O God, how is that supreme digit (kalā) which consists of a single syllable?
How does she, who is one, exist as many and in manifold forms?
Or rather, O Maheśvara, your very manifestation is indeed of many divisions.
"O Supreme Lord, by means of which may I be freed from doubt?
Having heard this,
Bhairava— the supreme one, the sole means for pacifying the terrible cycle of existence— immediately spoke these verses:
Bhairava said:
Listen, for I shall speak as I have been impelled by you;
it is a supreme secret, incomparable, and difficult even for the lords of the gods to obtain.
She who is all-pervading and subtle, the power that is the cause of Bhairava—
the Goddess whose essence is the letters of the alphabet and whose nature is aesthetic relish (rasa), yet who is not colored by the vowels;
she is neither Parā, nor Paśyantī, nor Madhyamā, nor Vaikharī.
She is known as the bursting and piercing of the crown, possessing the very nature of speech;
she is the Goddess consisting of the ninefold Vidyā, for she is not composed of Nāda, nor is she the Bindu or Kalā; she is neither all-pervasive nor devoid of meaning.
She is not rooted in the wheel-base, nor is she the fire-drill at the mouth of the channel;
she is not supported by the three voids, nor is she composed of the ninefold mantras.
She is neither white, nor red, nor yellow, nor black.
She is neither red nor tawny, nor indeed variegated;
that Goddess is not even possessed of a fraction of radiance.
She has neither sound nor touch, nor indeed form or taste.
She is neither scent, nor the senses, nor the instruments of action;
she is neither the lower nature, nor the Supreme Sovereign Goddess who is higher than the highest.
She is neither light, nor vigor, nor the power of accomplishment, nor even a mere fraction (kalā).

She is not primordial matter (*pradhāna*), nor is she the power of time (*pūṣṇatva*); she is neither knowledge (*vidyā*) nor the sacred tradition (*āgama*). She is not time (*kāla*), nor is she a fraction of time (*kalā*); she is neither destiny (*niyati*) nor the regulator (*niyāmikā*).

She is neither illusion (māyā) nor the Great Illusion (mahāmāyā), neither knowledge (vidyā) nor the notion of purity; she is not the Lord (īśvara), nor is she called Dākṣāyaṇī, nor is she Śakti, nor is she Śiva;
she is neither asleep nor awake, O Goddess, neither inert nor sluggish.
She has no form, no appearance, no elements, and no leaders;
she is not a genus, nor a place, nor a body, nor radiant;
she is not of the nature of desire or anger, and she neither dies nor lives.

O Beloved, she is neither the waking state nor the dreaming state, nor indeed is she the state of deep sleep. She is not the fourth state (turya), nor the state beyond the fourth (turyātīta); she is never the state of being established in the physical body (piṇḍastha). She is not established in the word (padastha), nor established in form (rūpastha), nor even is she that which transcends form (rūpātīta).
She is the Buddha, the Awakened, the Fully Enlightened; she is never here as an *īśvarī*.
She is not indeed the goddess *Pracayā*, for she is not that *Pracayā* known to me. She is perfected through supreme cessation (*paranivṛtti*), and does not possess the form of external cognition.
She is neither Śūnyā nor Āmisā, nor is she Hautrī or Vāgeśī; she is not even the triple Vedas (Trayī).
She is not called Bhargaśikhā, nor is she Khaśolkā Maheśvarī.
She is neither Ahaṃsī, nor Ānandā, nor indeed Nirānandā.
She is not a Yoginī, nor a Devī; she is not Śakti, nor Karaṅkiṇī.
She is not Kālī, nor Kaṅkālī, nor the seventeen-syllabled one.
She is neither monosyllabic nor polysyllabic, nor is she of the nature of a net.
She does not run, she does not stand, she does not weep, nor is she talkative;
she is neither distracted nor deeply contemplative, for she is like a lamp that has been extinguished.
She is not Brahmā, nor is she Viṣṇu, nor Rudra, nor Īśvara.
She is not Sadāśiva, O Goddess; she is not she whose form is unattached.
She is not Suṣumṇā; she is not that Goddess Siddhayogeśvarī.
She is neither Cāmuṇḍā, nor Mahocchuṣmā, nor Karālā, nor Daṃturā.
Neither Raktā, nor Caṇḍākṣī, nor Viccā, nor Bhairavī;
neither Ghoreśī, nor Viśveśī, nor Viśvā, nor Ghoranāyikā.
She is not Raudrī, nor Bhaṃbhottī, nor is she Harṭāhaṭṭāyudhā;
she is not Ṛkṣakarṇī, nor Caṇḍeśī, nor indeed Naṣṭeśvarī;
she is not Brāhmī, nor Māheśvarī, nor Kaumārī, nor Vaiṣṇavī.
Neither Vārāhī, nor Śāṅkarī, nor Viccā, nor Carvikā; neither Sāmyā, nor Kauverī, nor Vāruṇī, nor Samīraṇī;
neither Āgneyī, nor Aiśānī, nor Nairṛtī, nor Sūrpajā.
She is not Somajanakāpālī, nor Gāruḍī, nor Bharūṭikā;
she is not Nārasihī, nor Rudrāṇī, nor Bhairavavallabhā; she is not to be known as any one of the Sāhīs, nor indeed is she Jvālāmukhī.
She is not Khinkhinī, nor the mother of heroes, nor Śivādūtī, nor is she one who perishes.
For she is not the goddess in the form of a weapon, nor is she indeed Ḍāmarikā.
She is neither Jayā, nor Vijayā, nor Jayantī, nor Aparājitā.
She is not Dūtī, nor is she Kiṅkarī; she is not Sāṅkuśarūpiṇī.
She is not the goddess Vāgīśvarī, nor is she the one named Kuṇḍalā. She is not Maṅgalā, nor is she Nityā, nor indeed is she Ratneśvarī.
Neither the right nor the left, neither the east nor the west;
neither above nor Pātāla, neither Naya nor Vinaya;
neither Kulakaula nor Ātantra, neither Atimārga nor Lākula.
She does not transcend the Siddhānta, nor the Kāruka, nor the Vaimala;
she is neither the Vedānta, nor the Sāva, nor its ancillaries (aṅgas).
She is declared to be nameless, waveless, and undisturbed.
In the great city of the fire of thought and reflection, she is manifested in her own essential nature.
She is that essential nature; that is her true form; she is this and that; she is indeed that very one.
As the supreme destroyer of the insentient, she is consciousness itself, shining forth from within.
Everything that has been previously described was created by her;
O Goddess, she herself is never created by any object whatsoever.
Since there is nothing that exists apart from her, I am the Lord of all.
(216b) O Great Goddess, within this very world, which consists of both differentiated and non-differentiated natures,
that which has been declared as its true nature from the mouth of the Guru is indeed that alone.
O beautiful lady, he who acts having attained certainty is called Bhairava;
otherwise, his state as a bound soul (paśu) does not cease.
For this reason, O Goddess, this is proclaimed as the Mudrā.
Everything from Śiva down to the earthly realm is sealed by her.
The Great Mistress is changeless, waveless, and beyond mind;
she is indivisible, without abode, and whose very nature is without support.
O Goddess, she whose form is an unbroken circle, comparable to the full ocean—
everything previously described,
O fair-browed one, unfolds from her; what other entity exists within the belly of the world?
O Goddess, that which is pervaded by her has no end, nor does that which is within it;

she is the one whose form is the universe, who has gone everywhere, the Mistress of the universe, and the garlanded with the universe. She is eternally present, never far away, for she is one's own nature, though formless.
Knowing that liberation belongs to the living, otherwise it is meaningless;
by merely knowing this, O Goddess, one should always accomplish through *haṭha* whatever object exists within the sphere of Śiva and the earth.
Even if he does not desire them, the riches of this practitioner come to him by force—
those which are always difficult to attain even for Brahmā and the other gods, O Supreme Goddess—
in whatever region, city, or town that mortal dwells.

O Supreme Goddess, that which leads each being to liberation swiftly— whether by sight or even by touch— even immobile things touched by you attain union with Śiva; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
To you alone they offer salutations as the foremost goal, the supreme support of mantras,
the incomparable source of knowledge, the fuel for the fire of yoga,
and the rays of light that the perfected ones (siddhas) always revere.
The splendor of liberation constantly unfolds for him who possesses this knowledge within his body through the grace of the teacher’s mouth.
There is no doubt that such a person shall be endowed with all accomplishments (*siddhi*). Relying upon this excellent path, the Goddess of Knowledge (*Vidyā*), who embodies various forms,
assumes diverse manifestations and bestows the fruits of manifold accomplishments.
She is one, possessing all forms, conjoined with mudrās and maṇḍalas;
yet she is spread out here among these [beings] due to the diversity of mental states.
This which has been explained to you according to the essential meaning of the scriptures is indeed indescribable.
O Goddess of Gods, that which is written in a book, having passed from mouth to mouth, is never [fully realized];
its essence, filled with various fruits, is obtained from the mouth of the Guru.
Devoid of all mantras and the like, it is eternally perceived as perfectly peaceful and intensely radiant.
O Girijā, where there is no wound, all secrets would fall away; what more can I say to you now, who reside within the innermost core of my heart?
Thus, in the *Bhairavasrotas*, in the *Vidyāpīṭha*, in the *Śiraccheda* of the *Jayadrathayāmala*, the great tantra of twenty-four thousand verses, in the third hexad.

[The Chapter on Ritual Procedure] Having heard this, Girijā, her body bristling with horripilation, prostrated before Bhairava and uttered this hymn aloud: [The Chapter on Ritual Procedure] Having heard this, Girijā, her body bristling with horripilation, prostrated before Bhairava and uttered this hymn aloud.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of the Gods, you have declared an incomparable secret,
by which the Lords of Knowledge (Vidyeśvaras) and the others were deprived [of it] and fell into blindness."
Today, O Lord, I am liberated; I am freed from delusion, O observer of vows. I stand here, O Supreme Ruler, by your grace—what wonder is there in this!
Salutations to you, the heroic abode, the waveless one, the wielder of the trident.
Homage always to the all-pervading one; homage to the form of dissolution.
O Bull-bannered Lord, homage always to those who are the eight Lords of Knowledge.
Homage to the protector who dwells in the secret place; homage to you of many forms!
Homage to the one whose garment is a skeleton; homage to you, the Lord of the Nadīs!
Homage to the supremely pure; and homage to the destroyer of rebirth!
Salutations to You whose form is consciousness; salutations to You whose supreme power is consciousness. Salutations again and again to You, the destroyer of darkness, delusion, and great affliction.
Salutations to Kāma, the beloved; salutations to You who bear Your beloved as half of Your own body.
Homage to the steadfast one, to the hero; homage to him who moves with a tumultuous roar.
Homage to him whose necklace is the lord of serpents, and to him who wears a crown of skulls.
Homage to him of the playful attire, and homage to him who wanders at will through thought.
Salutations to you, Hiraṇyaretas, who possess a supreme form; salutations to you, who abide within the Bindu and Nāda, and for whom the celestial river is the beloved;
salutations to you, whose nature transcends the six knots and who are worthy of praise.
Salutations to the one tawny with flames, who is absorbed in meditation, whose form is like that of a swan-winged vehicle;
salutations to the one who is intensely longing, who is exceedingly subtle, and whose form is slow-moving.
Salutations, salutations to the one who dwells within the ocean of the scriptures; salutations to the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Salutations to you who abide on the six paths; salutations to Rudra, the wielder of the trident.
Salutations to you, the end-maker of Smara; salutations, repeated salutations, to the end-maker of Time.
O Supreme Lord, I am satisfied by your grace; what wonder is there in this?
Even now I have a doubt: how does she move by the division of steps?
O Lord, how does she grant success, and how is her division concealed?
O Lord of Gods, O best of deities, I wish to know this.
Having thus heard this hymn falling from the lotus-like mouth of his beloved, the Lord, with a delighted mind, spoke these words at once. Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess of the gods, to that which is wonderful along with its secret, just as I have been urged by you; I shall relate it exactly so,
O beloved, beginning from the time it was first broken by me with my hand and foot in solitude.
Then Śivā Nirmāṇasundarī, mounted upon the Bindu-cave,
stands as the Dharma-nature of Śambhu; she is the Pārameśvarī together with her power.

The cause of manifestation and the like arises precisely from the production of the aggregate (*samavāya*). Through the forms of rising and swelling, the Goddess has spread through as many words as there are vowels; thereafter, she is the cause residing within the wheel (*cakragā*).
From that, it is primarily the locus; from that, it is designated by the term "void.
Therein, among the seventy-two thousand channels, it illuminates through the most excellent states, which manifest in sequence with radiant light.
O God and Goddess, through the differentiation of words and the various functions of speech and phonemes,
she who is garlanded with a thousand syllables is then divided by her feet;
she is manifested as Śakti with reverence, both in her essential form and in her diverse manifestations.
The Supreme Goddess is not divided by nature, even though she appears as distinct through the limiting conditions of various attainments (*siddhi*);
yet, O Beloved, as long as the expansion and contraction [of consciousness] are not known by the individual (*nara*), she appears as differentiated according to those various attainments.
How can accomplishment be established through the distinction of individual knowledge?
When the Mistress of the Yogic Circle is known by her own radiance and power, through the various distinctions of supports and so forth, then accomplishment is held in the palm of one's hand.
When the practitioner, established within the three voids and unwavering in the union of the abodes (*dhāma*),

becomes the Lord of the Wheel (*cakranātha*), it is indeed so, and there is nothing marvelous in it. O Goddess, when [the breath] is within the belly of the *kanda*, in that auspicious and excellent six-rayed [lotus]...
Then Vīreśvara becomes manifest through the knowledge of mantra;
when he stands within the Vajra family as the beholder of the radiance of the state,
at the very moment of the cessation of one state after another, that *kalā* is manifested.

When Kuṇḍalinī has moved into that which consists of the power of Śiva (śiva-śakty-ātmake), vibrating and spreading through the waves [of consciousness], then that manifest aspect (kalā) is manifested.
When she rests upon the couch of the intellect (buddhi-talpavilāsinī) within the camp of her own nature (svabhāva-śivire).
When conjoined with her own radiant Lord by means of her own embrace,
all the Buddhas are then manifested through the power of that movement. (218b)

When the Mountain (Giri), situated upon the hanging wheel (*laṃbaka-cakra*), caresses the filaments (*kiṃjalka*), then that digit (*kalā*) which is the joy of the gods is manifested by those filaments. When [the practitioner] is intensely longing for the excellent Guru... *//* (ra)lālasaḥ.
When one describes the vibration of the Hero (*vīraspanda*), then that *kalā* is manifested;
joined with the fire of the state of consciousness (*cidbhāva*) through the touch of the equinox (*viṣuva*),
and intent upon the opening of the key (*kuñcikodyāṭana*), then that *kalā* is manifested.
When the tenfold [deity] is present in the ten forms within the *cinicini-cakra*,
then that *kalā* (creative power), whose nature is to spread forth, becomes manifest.
When the *rūpi-īśvarī* (the embodied sovereign) has unfolded in three ways within the *cakras*, [then that power is likewise revealed].
Then that digit is manifested when the playful Bindu shines within the radiant Kalāmālinī;
then that digit is manifested as the lotus-marked one blossoms.
When, in the bright golden age, the slayer of a Brahmin is intent upon the expansion and contraction of the radiant gold,
then that art is manifested;
when he is free from the skeleton and takes refuge in the small ball at the foot.
Then that digit (kalā) becomes manifest when it has ascended ten million-fold in the form of sound;
when it is dissolved in the heart-lotus within the three-fold aggregate (tripiṇḍa) that radiates in three ways;
and when the three fires are cast into the thirty [deities], then that digit becomes manifest.
In the untimely, in the deficient time, at the end of time, in the abode of Time—
when that vast Time of times is manifested, then indeed what [is there]?
[She is] Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, who holds a discus resplendent with sixteen moons.

Illuminated by the thirteen suns and endowed with the three fires, resting upon the radiant foundation in the state of *tāsu*, and agitated by the sequence of emission and withdrawal; mounted upon the sequence of the time of maintenance, while the night of emanation unfolds.
Then, having descended in such a form,
that power manifests itself within the house of fear, laughter, terror, touch, anger, and grief. (219a)
When that which is joyful remains clearly and very firmly established within the joyless,
then, O fortunate one, that supreme *kalā* manifests;
from which she knows— within the house of laughter, fear, touch, anger, and sorrow— that which is to be known.
When He remains clearly manifest and perfectly stable within the bliss of the threefold bliss,
then, O highly fortunate lady, that supreme digit (kalā) is revealed.
That by which one knows and that which one knows is His very body.
When one is firmly established therein in rightness, then that power (kalā) is manifested.
Since it is from there that the arising of birth and lineage occurs, and into that it dissolves,
when one is established in that [state] where it goes, then that power is manifested.

When the Radiance (bhāsā) resides within the Solar Family (bhānu-kula), and the Destroyer of the Solar Family (bhānu-kulāntaka) abides in the state of a blazing fire, then that digit (kalā) is manifested. When [the deity] who devours the splendor of the Fire of Time (kāla-vahni-prabha) resides in the support of the Fire of Time (kālānala-ādhāra)...
That lord of heroes also swallows it; then that digit is manifested.
And when, in the abode of the fierce family, the thousand-rayed sun has spread forth—that terrifying time of death—then that digit is manifested.
When that which is called birth, the destroyer of all and the ender of the lineage,
has fully developed within its supreme womb, then that digit is manifested. thaghaghathaghathaghathatha
In this very way, the world undergoes both destruction and emergence within him.
That power (kalā) residing within the lineage of the Kulānta is manifested by him—
that radiance known as the "Light of the Universe" (viśvabhāsā), in which time is proclaimed.
She in whom everything is situated through me is considered the Thousand-Syllabled One; she by whom this entire universe, along with the spheres of the elements and the maṇḍala,
is pervaded— she who is the Mudrā, the Vidyā, and filled with the Gaṇas— is considered the Thousand-Syllabled One.
Because it does not perish, it is the Imperishable (akṣara);

because it is devoid of both the perishable and the imperishable, it consists of all letters (sarvākṣaramayī). Therefore, it is composed of a thousand syllables, through the division of its quarters and the division of its constituent parts.
(219b) This Mistress of the Gods has been described—she who is difficult to be known even by the best of gods. What else shall I tell you? Speak, O Sovereign of all Sovereigns!
Thus, in the Bhairava-stream, in the Vidyāpīṭha, in the Śiraccheda, in the Jayadrathayāmala Mahātantra, in the twenty-four thousand [verse] work, in the third Ṣaṭka,
this is the chapter titled "The Procedure for Describing the Nature of the Goddess.
Having heard this, that Goddess was satisfied and blissful with the nectar of contentment.
Having prostrated before the Lord of the Asuras, whose commands are cherished upon his crown,
the Goddess spoke these words of profound meaning once again.
The Goddess said:
O Lord of the Gods, this secret which has been spoken by you is thus understood by me correctly;
now tell me,
O All-pervading One, how that supreme Kālī is the one who effects the dissolution of the universe?
How has Bhadrā descended? How does she perform creation?
How is Kālī the sustainer, and how is she the bringer of dissolution? How is she established in the multitude of light? This I wish to know.
"O Lord, this has been indicated by you many times, but not clearly explained.
I wish to hear it all; please speak out of your grace, O Bhairava.
Having heard this, he suddenly spoke with a loud laugh:
Bhairava, the destroyer of the god of love, who attains the playful grace of the crest-garlands of the hosts of the lords of the gods, said:
"Listen attentively; I shall fully declare that which is the true and supreme knowledge."
O fortunate one, that which was previously stated in this scripture at great length, I shall not describe here in detail; listen for a moment, O lotus-petal-eyed one.
This must be kept secret, O auspicious lady; even at the cost of one's life, the Guru should impart it [only to the worthy].
If, however, it is explained in an improper manner, Bhairava will surely become greatly agitated.
Therefore, one who desires his own welfare should practice the sequence in every way according to the yoga. O auspicious lady, this which you ask at this favorable moment is of two kinds.

It is waveless, transcending the family lineages, unique, and the bestower of supreme accomplishment; it is free from both the worshipped and the worshipper, and devoid of causes, logical reasons, and examples.
This is the inexpressible, the supreme essence of that sequence.
But there is another great distinction involving the worshiper and the object of worship;
it has been described in many ways by various [teachers], O lady of auspicious face.
I shall tell a wondrous tale, most marvelous and accompanied by its secret,
which is liberated from all states of being and devoid of the positions of existence and non-existence;
it is free from both being and non-being, and lies beyond the scope of the means of valid cognition.
Beyond speech, waveless, transcending conceptualization and motionless;
completely full, eternally satisfied, perfectly extinguished, and profoundly tranquil;
having the form of an indivisible circle, it is overflowing with supreme bliss.

Śiva is all-pervading, omnipresent, and beyond all causes; he is the supreme Brahman, whose nature is consciousness, the wondrous abode Bhairava. He is the omniscient creator of all, yet devoid of all designations.
By its light, that armor [of consciousness] becomes slow in the arising of its own vibration;
that radiant stream of light is Bhairavī, whose nature is luminosity.
O Bhairavī, she is the cause of the manifestation of the entire wheel of powers (śakticakra).
By this [power], the supreme *kalā* that brings an end to all that is to be manifested shines forth;
it is a radiant, blazing splendor, possessing the form of the crest of the supreme sun.
That supreme [splendor] resides in the highest enemy [of darkness], and by it, the enemy [of darkness] is utterly illuminated.
There, the radiant Rāri shines forth, liberated from all manifestation (bhāsā).
Therein, Rāri consists of those very lights: the Śākta, the Śāmbhava, and the Āṇava. Hence arises the emergence of the Sun; hence, through manifestation (bhāsā), there is the dawning of the Kalās.
The wheel of fire, the wheel of water, and the wheel of joy are illuminating;
the light that illuminates these is born from the inherent union with Śiva.

She is declared to be the light of consciousness (cidbhāsā), from which the wheel shines forth. O Sovereign of the Gods, nothing whatsoever exists there that is not joined with Speech (vāc). May that light shine as the light, the Kundalinī who moves through the light.
That abode possesses the vigor of the sun (*sārkavīrya*), the vigor of vision (*dṛṣṭivīrya*), and the vigor of the self (*sātmavīrya*).
Therein resides the sun within the fire-drill (*araṇi*); its radiance is its own essential form.
When that abode shines by means of the essential form of that [radiance], then its own true nature becomes manifest.
Then the lord of practitioners, possessing knowledge of the sequence of manifestations (*bhāsā-krama*), shines forth.
Within that, there is a group of four, and within that group of four, there is that [same reality].
This should be understood as non-different through the reasoning derived from the mouth of the Guru.
O Goddess, this sequence beginning with that has been described as the "Illumination" (bhāsā).
This must not be disclosed to one who is dull-witted or lacks proper examination.
O beautiful one, he who is by nature a great hero is a partaker of this Illumination.
"The Supreme Lord’s command is that the sequence of rays should be imparted to him. [End of] the Procedure for the Sequence of Radiance.
Now, I shall further proclaim this other supreme secret.
This secret, more secret than the secret, well-guarded and destructive of evil,
by the mere knowledge of which one shines here as Bhairava—
that radiance previously described, whose nature is the true essence of Śiva.
She, whose form is the essence of the wheel of radiance and whose nature is throbbing remembrance,
has descended in her own true form through the sequence of one,
two, and three; she is fourfold, fivefold, sixfold, and sevenfold.
The Goddess is eightfold, ninefold, and consists of ten and eleven;
indeed, as Rudra-Raudrīśvarī, she exists in an elevenfold form.
Kālī, moreover, should be known as twelvefold, consisting of the twelve suns, and then thirteenfold.
O Dear One, the sixteenfold [practice] consisting of ten and five is again correctly [established];
furthermore, it has descended in its own form as the seventeenfold.
The light previously described is the unfolding of the wheel of the self-luminous consciousness;
it is the throbbing reality in its own nature, possessing a function whose essence is that light.
It is the state of abiding and manifestation of the perfectly full essential nature.
The sequence of descent is subtle, having the form of an unbroken circle.
By that vigor, one who effects the descent through a form corresponding [to the goal] establishes the state of the gross and subtle stages in this sequence, O Mistress of the Gods.
The subtle has been described, as well as the gross division beginning with Bhairava;
O Maheśvarī, when the entire wheel of powers (śakticakra) reaches its limit at the stream (dhārā),
she should be known through that sequence as having the nature of the descent (avatāra).
The Sun should be made to shine within that [vision], and that [vision] arises from within the Sun.
Therefore, at that time, vision is vision; for that vision is indeed higher than the vision of vision.
That is the function (*vṛtti*), that is the vigor (*vīrya*), that is the function, and that alone is its manifestation, O beautiful one.
Thus, O slender-waisted one, she has descended as the manifestation of her own essential nature;
situated between the giving and the taking, she dwells in the midst of light and bliss.
She indeed takes the form of a swaying earring and resides within the moon, the sun, and the fire.
O Goddess, this attainment of the sequence shall then become like Bhairava himself.
Following this very sequence, that which resides in the mouths of the Yoginīs and has come down through the succession of gurus has been revealed to you today.
The *Mahāsamayavardha* should not be given to just anyone;
it must be protected at all costs as something more precious than life itself, and it should not be given to an animal-initiate (*paśu-dīkṣita*).
It is the great secret situated within [the heart], the beloved of Mahābhairava.
The Ritual Procedure for the Sequence of Descent.
Now I shall fully proclaim another secret, most wonderful,
which has not been told to anyone— the unsurpassed sequence of emanation.
Having attained which, the great hero is honored by the hosts of sky-faring goddesses;
this incomparable secret was spoken by Mahābhairava.
Having attained which, the great hero is honored by the hosts of sky-faring goddesses.
(221b) This incomparable secret was spoken by Mahābhairava;
and that which was previously taught, O Goddess, is the unbroken wheel of speech.
In that regard, there is the establishment of manifestation through the light of one's own essential nature.
Due to the stabilization of the light of consciousness and its perfect,
intense radiance, the entire circle of the cosmic egg (*aṇḍamaṇḍala*) is perfectly filled by that very body.
May he, who maintains his course like a seed whose ritual action has been performed,
who is supremely full of great delight, who is perfectly complete and radiant; may that Kālī, whose face is playful with saliva and who possesses a steady sun, be present.
Bhairavī, the sovereign of Bhairava, is mounted upon the digit at the end of the lotus;
established on the true path, she effortlessly creates seven,
eight, nine, eleven, and again twelve [worlds] upon that true path.
By means of the thirteen-fold synthesis, the sixteenth is indeed the fire-drill of the Kula;
and the seventeenth, O Mistress of the Gods, establishes and withdraws the sixfold state and the triad as one—
the radiant Bhavamālinī.
Then that Lalitā Bhāsā is remembered as the one who effects creation and maintenance.
That by which [reality] was fragmented, fragmented again—that very thing was fragmented by him.
When Kālī is indeed unfragmented, she is neither fragmented nor mounted upon a cat.
Then that "khaṇḍanā" is not a fragmentation at all, but rather a falling away from anything else;
for when one is established in the unbroken circle (*akhaṇḍamaṇḍala*) and remains undivided everywhere,
then Kālī, whose form is *nithyū* [the state beyond duality], is the playful goddess who delights in the sport of creation.
When she abides in the state of Time beyond time, the auspicious Kālikā brings about the dissolution of all that belongs to Time;
together with the Hūhūkas, she emits the entire cosmic egg.
When she has ascended to the station of Anāśrita and shines forth through its creative activity, [she manifests].
Then she shines forth as light, free from the limiting adjuncts of objective cognition;
having created that [universe], the Mistress of the Gods, whose nature is the play of functional activity, returns to it.
Being present within that, she vomits forth the true essence of Mahābhairava.
Then Bhairava, the source of Bhairava, emits the sixfold Bhairava— six-cornered, consisting of six kalās,
and exceedingly fierce— as the Lord of the Six Groups (Ṣaṭkanātha), who is radiant.
That [power], whose nature is that activity, has the form of the intermediate *raudra*;
she vomits forth that Great Preta Sadāśiva, the Lord of Khaṭvāṅga.
She flashes forth as the Great Jewel, intent on fulfilling that purpose.
Through that activity, she effortlessly emits the entire manifestation of mantra;
then, resorting to a radiant and fierce state,
this fierce mistress of all mantras emits the Lord.
Though it was shining and throbbing with the intense wildness of that activity,
that fierce power again vomited forth Rudra situated within the *kalaśa*.
Or rather, she [vomited] Rudra three hundred times by means of the abode of the three worlds.
By means of the union with the radiance of its own activity, it should fill the entire universe.
Having thus cast off her burden, that created power, becoming agitated,
vomits forth Viṣṇu once more— a fierce and turbulent fire.
When there is great delight in the house of nectar, reeling with the exuberance of worldly activity,
and when Kālī appears as hunger once more, she then vomits forth with force the most terrible Brahmacakra, which resounds with the exuberance of the Vedas.
Then, from the supreme Nāda, he vomited forth Hāṭakeśvara—
the God who delights in the great divine play, the Lord of Rati, possessed of great power,
mounted upon Kāma, attached to Kāma, and situated within the center of a six-cornered interior.
Terrible, situated in the midst of the six powers, and pervaded by six rays—
having caused the expansion of its rays, she indeed becomes most fierce;
for she has vomited forth the entire Kālāgnirudra from her own essential nature.
Like the agitation of fish turning about in the spreading fragrance of its movement,
he again [created] by that same [power] a great multitude of twelve suns;
and furthermore, a thirteenth, terrible one, known by the name Mārtaṇḍa.
Thus the Sūrya family was vomited out through the application of the *vṛtti* and *udgāra* [breaths];
then again, the moist *kalācakra*, radiant with the sixteen supports.
That which was vomited by Mahākālī, the Fortune of the Universe, consists of nectar.
Furthermore, there is the threefold terrible fire with seven tongues, fearsome and intent upon filling its own functions;
beyond that is the Vāḍava fire.
In her own essential nature, she is joined with her own family of deities;
thus, having arisen as the Wheel of Light within the abode of the enclosures,
that formidable Ghorā dwells once more in the Wheel of Sound, which is difficult to approach.
Then, in the state of the Great Wind, when Bhairavī moves within the Mistress of the Ten Tanmātras, accompanied by the Lord of the Cakras,
then by that Goddess of gods, the unsurpassed Sparśacakra (Wheel of Touch) is attained.
When the form-cluster (*rūpakula*) is emitted together with its own rays and accompanied by the Lord of the Wheel (*cakkranātha*),
the beings are agitated within the three voids (*trivāmanisva*) in the nature of light (*bhārūpa*), and the faces of the Asuras are not [seen].
When that [form-cluster] is emitted, it is filled with hundreds of rays by her.
Accompanied by the Lord of Rays, consisting of thirty and twelve [parts],
moving through speech, neither failing nor deficient;
then at the end, the Vedas were born, the wheel of flavors that removes fear.
Accompanied by Kharaśminātha, [he is] fond of necklaces and the six flavors. Again, when the terrible times were agitated and the great [world] was well-nigh dead,
then by her the wheel of fragrance (gandhacakra), crowded with hundreds of supporting rays, [was manifested].
Accompanied by the Lord of his own circle, Bhairava, the support of his own circle,
was surrounded by a hundred great Mothers. Then, O slender-waisted one, she became agitated within the nectar-filled [vessel], and from that agitation, the wheel emerged and was vomited forth by her.
Endowed with hundreds of rays of sound, it churns the family of mental constructs (*saṃkalpa*).
Then, when the goddess Karaṅkiṇī was born from the light of the *ghoṭa*,
she spoke to the Lord of Action (*kṛtīśvara*) as she emerged, concerning the wheel (*cakra*).
